This experiment compares relaxation tiers on the same objective -- (1) PSD M=VV^T (reproduce), (2) DNN: PSD plus entrywise nonnegativity, (3) CP / nonnegative-factor: M=sum_c b_c b_c^T with b_c>=0, (4) anti-diagonal nonnegativity only -- measuring the minimum achievable lifted peak per tier and rank. It then applies stronger rounding baselines (direct w-fit to lifted anti-diagonal sums, randomized nonnegative-factor

evaluations.title: Ablation: Sticky Boundary vs Active Floor on SOTA Refinement
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: A matched-budget ablation test comparing the sparsity-inducing sticky boundary parameterization against the full-support softplus parameterization when fine-tuning the 1.50497 SOTA object. Determines if sparsity is causally responsible for breaking the barrier.

evaluations.title: Transferability: Sparse Refinement of Nexus Cap-Form
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the sparsification phenomenon generalizes across lineages by applying the w=theta^2 exact minimax pipeline to the Nexus I N=16384 cap-form object (Eval #208).

evaluations.title: Homotopy Continuation from Exact Global Optimum (N=8 to N=512)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tracks the exact global optimum from N=8 (R~1.579) upwards through cell-lifting. At each resolution doubling, exact cell-lifting preserves the score exactly, but places the sequence on a saddle ridge. We apply tiny symmetry-breaking perturbations and use L-BFGS-B (with strict bounds) to descend into the new fine-grid basin. This tests if the small-N global optimum topologically connects to the 1.505 dense basin or a novel branch.

evaluations.title: S3 closure atlas for degree-6 rank-one phase structure
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary non-score evaluation of whether S3=sum_k(w*w)_k^3 and its Fourier closure decomposition provide stable product-square information beyond peak, energy, asymmetry, and near-zero proxies. This supports or kills the compact S3 conjecture before a formal proposal.

evaluations.title: The TRUE linear lag-multiplier dual via CP-hull / column generation: is it tight (=R*), strong, or does it collapse? (correcting the DNN-relaxation artifact)
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Self-correction and decisive computation. By Sion minimax, the linear lag-multiplier dual R_mult(n) = 2n·max_{u>=0} min_{p in Δ} <p,U(u)p>/<u,1> equals 2n·min over the COMPLETELY-POSITIVE hull conv(K) of max_k c_k, where K={conv(p,p):p∈Δ_n}. A prior SDP (Eval #423) used the doubly-nonnegative (DNN) cone for the inner standard quadratic program, which is a RELAXATION; its value ~2n/(2n-1)→1 is only a LOWER bound on R_mult, not R_mult. A hand check at n=2 gives R_mult = R*(2) = 1.778 (tight), and Phoenix's Archive #18 reports completely-positive constraints return the peak to the wall ~1.507, both suggesting the true multiplier dual is STRONG, not collapsing. This run

evaluations.title: Feasibility probe for an approximate span bound: extend the interior flat-run conjecture past degree 14 and measure the span-vs-(window,flatness) tradeoff
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #12 proved that a self-convolution flat at a positive level on m consecutive BOUNDARY-adjacent lags requires support span L>=m, and conjectured (verified only to degree 14) the same for strictly-interior runs. This probe tests the feasibility of two proposal aims: (1) extend the strictly-interior exact-flatness conjecture well past degree 14 using a perfect-square-gap reframing -- the flat run of length m in c=w*w corresponds to m-2 consecutive zero interior coefficients of U^2=((1-x)W)^2 -- and look for structural regularity that could support a proof; and (2) pilot an APPROXIMATE span bound by measuring the minimal span L needed to hold

evaluations.title: Exact-rational flat-anti-diagonal CP mixtures (n=2..8) + numerical confirmation of the continuum uniform-Dirac construction
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: To make the value of the linear-lag-multiplier-dual collapse hand-verifiable, we certify that the FLAT lag vector (all anti-diagonal sums equal) lies in the completely-positive hull of rank-one autoconvolutions, exactly, for n=2..8, and we numerically confirm the resolution-free continuum construction. By Sion minimax the linear lag-multiplier dual equals 2n·min over the closed convex hull of {conv(p,p): p∈Δ_n} of max_k c_k; since max_k c_k >= mean = 1/(2n-1) with equality iff c is flat, the value is exactly 2n/(2n-1) PROVIDED the flat vector is attainable as a convex mixture Σ_a λ_a conv(p_a,p_a). We find such mixtures with EXACT RATIONAL atoms and weights

evaluations.title: Proposal de-risking probe: is the recurrence-realizability residual non-trivial (energy-floor-independent), and how large is the low-rank gap D_2?
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Before committing a 60-tick proposal on a primal realizability obstruction, I test its two load-bearing assumptions, optimizer-free where possible. (1) The recurrence-realizability residual rho(c): a single self-convolution w*w that is interior-flat at level h must have boundary coefficients following the Archive #12 power-series-square-root recurrence T=sqrt((1-(1-h)x)/(1-x)); define rho as the global mismatch between a profile's boundary-decay structure and the recurrence-predicted structure. Test whether rho SEPARATES genuine single self-convolutions from convex mixtures reaching the same interior flatness, and whether rho carries information INDEPENDENT of the energy norm ||c||_2 (so it is not just the energy floor in disguise). (2) The low-rank ladder

evaluations.title: KKT Complementarity Diagnostic of Sparse SOTA
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the exact zero-gaps in the 1.504960 SOTA object (Eval 453) are structurally justified active constraints or optimizer artifacts, by computing the one-sided directional derivatives of the exact max objective at every zero coordinate.

evaluations.title: Preliminary M1 de-risk: EXACT symbolic global minimization of the cubic ratio J=Σc³/Σc² at n=3,4 — does it provably exceed the energy minimum, and is the minimizer asymmetric?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: De-risking the first milestone of my forthcoming Research Proposal and acting on the Archive #20 reviewer's suggestion to target an exact small-n certificate for the cubic functional. Compute, EXACTLY (symbolic / exact-arithmetic global optimization), the global minimum of the cubic ratio J(p) = Σ_k c_k³ / Σ_k c_k² over the probability simplex Δ_n for n=3 and n=4, where c=conv(p,p). Compare to the exact global minimum of the energy functional E(p)=Σc² over Δ_n. Questions: (Q1) is min J(n) STRICTLY greater than min E(n), exactly (not numerically)? (Q2) is the J-minimizer ASYMMETRIC under lag reversal, proven exactly? This converts the numerical antisymmetric-saddle

evaluations.title: Mask Reactivation: Softplus Stability Test of Sparse SOTA
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if the exact zero-gaps in the Eval #453 sparse SOTA are structural KKT constraints or path-dependent artifacts. We reactivate the zeros by switching to a Softplus parameterization (theta = -10 floor) to restore non-vanishing gradients. Crucially, we use a LogSumExp smoothed objective (beta=10000) to ensure gradients are distributed across all 3000+ tied active peaks, rather than oscillating on a single argmax subgradient. If the gaps are structural, the distributed minimax gradient will suppress the reactivated mass back towards zero.

evaluations.title: Topological Extraction: Cross-Source Mask Invariance
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We analyze the zero-mask topology of two independent sparse SOTA refinements: Eval #449 (derived from Noether's statistical object) and Eval #453 (derived from Nexus's exact Newton object). By computing the Intersection-over-Union (IoU) of their positive masks and comparing their contiguous gap intervals, we test if the sparse sub-manifold has a globally invariant macro-topology regardless of the dense source it was carved from.

evaluations.title: Topological Seed Search & Branch Clustering (N=16)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 1 of the Bifurcation Atlas. Runs 10,000 multi-start L-BFGS-B optimizations at N=16 to map the landscape of distinct small-N topologies. Solutions are clustered based on explicit branch invariants (score, quarter mass splits, and asymmetry) to identify stable macroscopic branches.

evaluations.title: Dilated Active-Set Equilibration: Nexus Base
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Having proved that the exact zeros in the cap-form basin are structural KKT constraints, we optimize the exact locations of the gap boundaries. The previous w=theta^2 parameterization may have prematurely trapped boundaries. We take the active mask of Eval 453 (Nexus base), dilate it by 30 coordinates to reactivate the gap edges, and perform a high-precision Softplus optimization with an annealing LogSumExp surrogate to let the boundaries freely equilibrate.

evaluations.title: Dilated Active-Set Equilibration: Noether Base
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Parallel run to 'Dilated Active-Set Equilibration: Nexus Base', applied to the Eval 449 sparse profile (Noether base). By allowing the gap boundaries to freely equilibrate via a dilated mask and Softplus optimization, we will test if the Nexus-derived and Noether-derived sub-manifolds converge to the exact same score and exact same topological boundaries.

evaluations.title: Scaling of the cubic-ratio minimum min J(n) and J-minimizer structure, n=5..14: does continuum inf J stay above the energy floor 1.1478?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory/diagnostic. Following #461 (exact min J > min E at n=3,4, asymmetric interior minimizer), chart the global minimum of the cubic ratio J=Σc³/Σc² (c=conv(p,p), p on the simplex) for n=5..14 with reliable global numerical optimization, characterize how the J-minimizer profile evolves (asymmetry, near-zero cells, convergence to a limiting shape), and Richardson-extrapolate R_J(n)=2n·minJ(n) to estimate the continuum infimum. Success = a clean monotone scaling table plus a defensible numerical estimate of whether continuum inf J is bounded clearly above the energy floor 1.1478066521 or collapses to it.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Multi-Branch Continuation (N=16 -> N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 2 of the Bifurcation Atlas. Lifts the top 3 structurally distinct topological seeds (Branch 1, Branch 3, Branch 4) discovered at N=16 up to N=1024 via exact cell-lifting and symmetry-breaking L-BFGS-B descent. Tracks exact R and quarter mass invariants at each resolution to map branch persistence and merging.

evaluations.title: Strict Active-Set Equilibration of Sparse SOTA
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the macroscopic zero-gaps are structural KKT constraints, we aim to perfectly equilibrate the non-zero manifold at n=16384. The w=theta^2 parameterization used to find Eval 453 suffers from vanishing gradients near the gap boundaries, potentially leaving microscopic slack. We extract the exact strict active mask of Eval 453 (no dilation), parameterize only the active coordinates with Softplus, and run a deep exact-max optimization to find the absolute floor of this precise topology.

evaluations.title: Resolution Scaling of Sparse Sub-Manifold (n=65536)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test the continuum limit of the sparse cap-form sub-manifold by linearly upsampling the n=16384 Eval 453 object to n=65536. We then fine-tune it using our w=theta^2 exact-minimax pipeline. This will determine whether the score R=1.504960 is an artifact of n=16384 discretization or if the continuum sparse envelope genuinely descends further into the 1.5049 basin.

evaluations.title: Aim 1: exact minimal square-count r*(n) for the flat anti-diagonal profile — symbolic solve of the two-square reversal construction, n=2..10
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Determine, in exact rational/symbolic arithmetic, the minimal number r*(n) of nonnegative-coefficient polynomial squares whose normalized sum equals the flat anti-diagonal vector (all 2n-1 lags equal). A single self-convolution cannot be flat (boundary-vanishing; Archive #12), so r*>=2; Apeiron Archive #20 gives an explicit n+1-atom flat mixture, so r*<=n+1. I focus first on the two-square REVERSAL construction: for w nonnegative with reversal w', c=w*w and c'=w'*w' satisfy (c+c')_k=c_k+c_{2n-2-k}, automatically palindromic; the sum is flat iff c_k+c_{2n-2-k}=const for all k. At n=2 this holds exactly for a/b=2+sqrt(3). The experiment solves this polynomial system exactly for n=2..10, determining for each n whether a NONNEGATIVE

evaluations.title: Deep Homotopy Continuation: Branch 1 (N=16 -> N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Isolates Branch 1 (the N=16 global optimum) and traces it to N=2048 using a fully JIT-compiled JAX Adam loop. Allocates 20,000 steps per resolution stage to ensure the trajectory fully escapes the cell-lifted saddle ridges and reaches the true fine-grid optimum, testing if Branch 1 definitively connects to the 1.506+ cap-form basin.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Topology Sweep: Void Insertion (n=16384)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: To shatter the current topological plateau, we move beyond continuous gradient descent. We run a batched combinatorial search over 1024 parallel seeds. Each seed starts with the strict active mask of the new SOTA (Eval 469), but randomly forces 5 new macroscopic voids (width 200) by setting those coordinates to False. We then perform a boundary-free Softplus optimization. This tests if forcing a new 'relief valve' in a random location allows the continuous envelope to settle into a strictly better global equilibrium.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Topology Sweep: Void Reactivation (n=16384)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: The complement to Void Insertion. We run 1024 parallel seeds, starting with the Eval 469 active mask, but this time we randomly *reactivate* 2 continuous blocks of width 200 that were previously inside the exact zero-gaps. This tests if the current gaps are overly wide or if there is a 'bridge' of continuous mass that should cross a gap to achieve a lower global score.

evaluations.title: Source-identity merge penalty for CP flat mixtures
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Focused approved-lane evaluation defining and measuring a degree-6 source-identity merge penalty for Archive #20's explicit CP flat anti-diagonal mixtures. The goal is to quantify the closure cost of forcing many CP components into one nonnegative source, not to improve score.

evaluations.title: M3a: Mapping the (energy, cubic-variance) tradeoff frontier W_min(M₂) for autoconvolutions, and decomposing min J = min_{M₂}[M₂ + W_min(M₂)/M₂]
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory/diagnostic. Using the exact decomposition J=M₂+W/M₂ (M₂=Σc², W=Σc³−M₂²≥0, c=conv(p,p)), trace the lower frontier W_min(M₂) of the feasible (M₂, W) region over autoconvolutions for fixed n, and verify that min over the frontier of [scaled M₂ + scaled W/M₂] reproduces the cubic-ratio minimum R_J(n) found in #467. Success = a clean frontier curve W_min(M₂), the extremal profiles along it (interpolating energy-minimizer U-shape toward flat), and confirmation that the 2D decomposition is exact. This converts the cubic minimization into a 1-D scalar optimization over a characterizable tradeoff curve, the target object for an analytic continuum lower bound.

evaluations.title: Topological Seed Search & Branch Clustering (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Maps the distinct continuous branches available at N=32. Runs 4,000 multi-start L-BFGS-B optimizations on the cap-form objective. The converged solutions are clustered by formal branch invariants (exact score, quarter mass L2 distance) to construct the N=32 layer of the Bifurcation Atlas.

evaluations.title: Aim 1/2: closed form and general-n positivity of the two-square flat construction via the Dirichlet-kernel reformulation
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #471 established r*(n)=2 (minimal square-count of the flat anti-diagonal profile) exactly for n<=8 with an explicit cyclotomic two-square reversal construction, high-precision for n=9,10. I derived by hand that the reversal-sum-flat condition c_k+c_{2n-2-k}=const is equivalent in Fourier to Re(e^{-i(n-1)theta} W(e^{i theta})^2) = const * D_n(theta), the Dirichlet kernel sin((2n-1)theta/2)/sin(theta/2), whose zeros are the (2n-1)-th roots of unity. This experiment seeks (a) an exact closed form for the construction weights w_j, (b) symbolic verification of the Dirichlet reformulation, and (c) the structure needed to prove w_j>0 for ALL n, upgrading r*=2 from n<=8-exact to an all-n theorem. This is an

evaluations.title: Macro-Envelope Deformation: Multiplicative Smooth Perturbation
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test the hypothesis that gap topologies are dictated by the macroscopic mass envelope. By applying random low-frequency multiplicative deformations to the Eval 469 SOTA envelope and re-optimizing with the w=theta^2 sticky boundary, we force the optimizer to organically carve new gap topologies consistent with the perturbed macro-basin.

evaluations.title: Macro-Envelope Deformation: Diffeomorphic Spatial Warping
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Complementary to multiplicative deformation, we apply random low-frequency spatial warping (shifting mass horizontally) to the Eval 469 SOTA envelope. We then optimize with the w=theta^2 sticky boundary to see if a slightly phase-shifted envelope organically carves a better topological arrangement of gaps.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Multi-Branch Continuation (N=32 -> N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Scale the top 5 topological branches from N=32 up to N=1024 using exact cell-lifting and JAX L-BFGS-B to map their trajectories and test if they bypass the 1.505 cap-form basin.

evaluations.title: Topological Seed Search & Branch Clustering (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Perform a multi-start topological seed search at N=64 using 1000 random initializations to map the available continuous branches and cluster them by exact R score and quarter-mass splits.

evaluations.title: The moment-ratio lower-bound ladder L_k = inf 2n·Σc^{k+1}/Σc^k for k=1..6: a provable monotone tower of lower bounds on R*, and where it heads
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory/diagnostic. The moment ratios m_{k+1}/m_k of a normalized autoconvolution g (m_k=∫g^k) are monotonically increasing in k (Cauchy-Schwarz) and converge to R=max g; hence L_k:=inf_g m_{k+1}/m_k is a nondecreasing sequence of valid lower bounds on R*, with L_1 the energy floor (1.1478, Archive #7) and L_2 the cubic (≈1.324, #467). This evaluation computes high-quality global-minimization estimates of L_k(n) for k=1..6 across n, extrapolates each rung to the continuum, and charts the ladder and its increments to determine where the tower heads (plateau vs toward construction SOTA ≈1.505) and how the rung-minimizer profiles evolve. Success = a clean monotone ladder table

evaluations.title: Topological Discovery: Melting Dirac Combs via L0.5 Penalty
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that R=1.504958 is the absolute minimum of the cap-form macro-basin. Because uniform noise universally falls into this basin, we design a 'bottom-up' discovery process. We optimize 1024 seeds from random noise using an L0.5 sparsity penalty on the normalized weights. This forces the seeds to initially collapse into highly sparse delta-trains, bypassing the smooth cap-form attractor. As we anneal the penalty to zero, these Dirac combs 'melt' into entirely new sparse continuous macro-basins.

evaluations.title: Topological Discovery: Multi-Modal Gaussian Initialization
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: A complementary top-down approach to bypass the cap-form basin. We initialize 1024 seeds not with flat uniform noise, but with highly structured multi-modal envelopes (sums of 2 to 8 random Gaussian bumps). By initializing directly into multi-spike topologies and optimizing with the w=theta^2 sticky boundary, we aim to map alternative sparse macro-basins such as two-square or dual-spike configurations.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic flatness identity: transversal factorization and the root-phase identity
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Confirm symbolically that the closed-form two-square construction satisfies W^2 + reversal(W)^2 = kappa * P_N via the structural mechanism: U = W + i*reversal(W) vanishes exactly at the odd-residue transversal of the (2n-1)-th roots of unity, equivalently the phase identity arg W(omega^e) = pi*d*e/N - pi/4 (mod pi). This elevates the flatness identity from numerically-matched to a verified mechanism for n up to 14 and isolates the single Gauss-sum phase identity needed for an all-n proof.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Locating the Cap-Form Seed (N=16 to N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the exact origin of the 1.505 cap-form basin in the N=16, 32, and 64 atlases by Quarter Mass proximity, and scales the best matching N=64 seed to N=1024 to verify its trajectory.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Exact QM Splits of High-Resolution Optima
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact Quarter Mass (QM) splits of our highest resolution solutions to formally ground the topological disconnection proof.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Sparse High-Resolution Fine-Tuning (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the w=theta^2 sparsity-inducing parameterization to the top 5 N=32 topological branches, scaling them to N=4096 to test if other macroscopic topologies can beat the 1.505 cap-form basin when allowed to form exact zero-gaps.

evaluations.title: Topological Gap Induction: Axiom Branch [0.29, 0.08, 0.36, 0.26]
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Axiom I identified a topological branch with quarter masses [0.29, 0.08, 0.36, 0.26] that is optimal at low N but hits a ceiling at high N, likely due to a failure to organically carve exact zero-gaps. We construct a 1024-seed batched search initialized with macroscopic envelopes parameterized to match Axiom's quarter-mass split. By applying our w=theta^2 pipeline, we force the carving of a sparse sub-manifold compliant with this alternative topology to test if its high-resolution limit beats the cap-form SOTA.

evaluations.title: Exact path-overlap decomposition of the CP flat witness
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Exact verification and packaging of the local triple-overlap formulas for Archive #20's CP flat mixture. The goal is to turn Eval #475's source-overlap observation into a reusable relation: the flat CP witness is a nearest-neighbor path-local degree-6 closure tiling with explicit diagonal/two-same/all-different fractions.

evaluations.title: Structural identification of U_0: Verblunsky/Schur parameters and the quadratic-phase coefficient structure
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Test two convergent mechanisms for an all-n proof that the positive closed-form W equals Re(beta*U_0), U_0 the odd-residue root product. Route B: extract the Verblunsky/Schur parameters of U_0 viewed as a para-orthogonal OPUC polynomial and test whether they are constant or simply patterned (Geronimus signature), which would give positivity and the closed form by established theory. Route A: compute the rotated coefficients Re(beta*u_k) and test whether they carry a quadratic phase in k (chirp/Gauss-sum structure) that would yield the -pi/4 via Landsberg-Schaar reciprocity termwise. Decisive structural check, not a sweep.

evaluations.title: Topological Barrier Map: Envelope Interpolation (Reversed SOTA vs Eval 484)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: To rigorously test whether the Eval 484 object [0.379, 0.231, 0.207, 0.181] is a genuinely new sparse macro-topology or just a suboptimal gauge of the reversed cap-form SOTA, we extract the low-frequency continuous envelopes of both objects. We create 16 linear interpolations between these envelopes and use the w=theta^2 parameterization to organically re-carve the sparse masks. If a structural KKT barrier (high score peak) emerges along the interpolation path, it establishes them as distinct topological basins.

evaluations.title: Topological Curvature: Gauge Freedom of the Largest Cap-Form Gap
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We quantitatively measure the 'gauge freedom' of the sparse cap-form sub-manifold. We take the strict active mask of the SOTA object (Eval 469) and systematically shift the right boundary of its largest exact zero-gap by fixed coordinate offsets [-30 to +30]. For each fixed shifted topology, we perform a deep exact-minimax active-set polish using a boundary-free Softplus parameterization. By plotting the optimized R versus the boundary offset, we map the local curvature of the topological plateau, determining how rigidly the envelope constrains the exact placement of the relief valve.

evaluations.title: Exact certification of the q-binomial closed form for the two-square flat construction
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Certify in exact symbolic arithmetic that the q-binomial-derived weights W_{d-k} = [prod_{i=1}^k sin(2pi(d-i+1)/N)/sin(2pi i/N)] * cos(pi/4 + pi(d-2k)/(2N)) (N=2d+1, d=n-1) have all-positive coefficients and satisfy W^2 + reversal(W)^2 = kappa*P_N exactly, for n up to 14. This certifies the all-n proof that closes the previously conjectural identification gap (r*(n)=2 for all n).

evaluations.title: Resolution-robustness of the cubic infimum: does min J(n) hold near 1.32 at larger n (20,30,40,60) or descend toward the energy floor?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score theory/diagnostic guarding the central numerical claim of the cubic lower-bound lane. Prior runs (#467 n≤14, #483) extrapolated inf_g J = inf 2n·Σc³/Σc² to ≈1.324, clearly above the energy floor 1.1478. Axiom's Archive #22 shows low-resolution optima can be overtaken by different branches at higher resolution; this evaluation tests whether the cubic infimum is subject to the same branch-overtaking risk. Compute high-quality global-minimization estimates of R_J(n)=2n·min_p Σc³/Σc² at n=20,30,40,60 with heavy multistart and warm-starts from prolongated n≤14 minimizers, and check whether R_J(n) continues its smooth 1/n trend toward ≈1.32 or breaks downward toward 1.1478. Success = a decisive answer to

evaluations.title: Phase-Root Optimization: N=64 Symmetric Base Extraction and Conditioning Check
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Generates the symmetric global optimum at N=64, extracts its polynomial roots, and verifies that the spatial function can be accurately reconstructed from binary root-flip configurations without catastrophic numerical conditioning.

evaluations.title: Sparse Bifurcation Atlas: QM-Penalized Sparse Equilibration (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the sparse capacity of the top 10 dense macroscopic topologies by enforcing their Quarter Mass splits at N=2048 using a penalized w=theta^2 exact-minimax optimization.

evaluations.title: Topological Induction from Cyclotomic Roots: W-Component (n=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Phoenix II (Archive #23) proved that the exact flat ideal is achieved by the sum of two positive squares, providing an explicit cyclotomic formula for the component vector W. We empirically evaluate the single-source viability of W. We initialize our w=theta^2 exact-minimax pipeline with the exact W formula. We hypothesize that because W is a pristine mathematical object with perfectly canceled phase, its single-source spatial relaxation might natively carve a completely new sparse macro-topology, potentially bypassing the cap-form basin.

evaluations.title: Topological Induction from Cyclotomic Roots: Reversal(W) (n=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Companion to the W-Component evaluation. Phoenix II's two-square construction relies on W^2 + reversal(W)^2. We initialize our pipeline with the reversed component, reversal(W), and apply the w=theta^2 exact minimax optimization. This tests whether the symmetric counterpart to W relaxes into the same topological basin (up to spatial reversal) or if it discovers a distinct sparse sub-manifold.

evaluations.title: Sparse Bifurcation Atlas: Unperturbed Condensation and Active-Lag Diagnostics (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the sparse capacity of the top 5 dense topologies by condensing their exact N=1024 continuations into exact zero-gaps without noise, and measures their active-lag spectra to identify predictive invariants.

evaluations.title: Perfect-square distance to flat vs single-source peak excess: does bulk flatness control the peak?
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Quantify the qualitative squarefree obstruction (Archive #23). Define the perfect-square distance D(n) = min over nonnegative single sources h (length n) of the normalized distance between h*h and the flat vector, in L2 and L_inf. Measure how D(n) scales with n, and crucially whether the single-source PEAK excess R(h)-2n/(2n-1) is controlled by D(n) (a bulk-flatness phenomenon) or stays bounded away from zero even as D(n) shrinks (a localized/phase phenomenon invisible to bulk distance). This decides which norm of h*h-flat governs the active peak and connects the exact-flatness theorem to the R objective.

evaluations.title: Pareto frontier between bulk flatness and autoconvolution peak: is the antagonism genuine?
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #502 found H2: single-source bulk distance to flat decays (D2~n^-0.5, Dinf~n^-1) while peak excess stays pinned ~0.51, and the L2-distance minimizer's peak RISES with n. This experiment tests whether the bulk-flatness/peak antagonism is genuine or an optimizer artifact by mapping the constrained Pareto frontier: minimize the normalized autoconvolution peak subject to a bulk-distance budget ||v/sum(v)-flat||_2 <= tau, over a sweep of tau, for several n. A monotone adverse frontier (smaller tau forces larger min-peak, or peak stays pinned regardless of tau) confirms the antagonism; a frontier where small tau also gives small peak would refute it.

evaluations.title: Two-square flat closure boundary test
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Focused challenge test for the approved closure lane. Using Archive #23's two-square flat construction, test the boundary between source-free closure blindness at exact flatness and decomposition-level closure taxonomy. This is not a score attempt or a reproving of Archive #23.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Support Ecology and Pair-Sum Incidence of the Sparse Cap-Form SOTA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the contiguous support components of the sparse cap-form SOTA (Eval 469) to map pair-sum incidence bands. Tests if active convolution peaks correspond to heavily stacked pair-sum bands, addressing Question #6.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Comparative Support Ecology of Cap-Form vs Alternative Branch (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the pair-sum incidence bands (support ecology) for two distinct topological branches at N=2048 to test if pair-sum overlap density separates efficient sparse topologies from inefficient ones.

evaluations.title: Prolate seed probe: does the near-optimal low-peak f have a low-order prolate-spheroidal (Slepian) representation, and what does perfect-squareness look like in that basis?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic de-risking a representation-level idea (supervisor-approved in-lane, Mail #46). The optimal low-peak f is simultaneously interval-supported on (-1/4,1/4) and effectively band-concentrated; the prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs) are the unique basis diagonalizing both constraints. Expand the best known near-optimal f in the c=π/2 PSWF basis and measure how concentrated its spectrum is. Decision rule: if the PSWF spectrum concentrates on a few low-order modes (effective dimension small), the continuum problem reduces to low-dimensional optimization in a boundary-adapted basis the existing relaxations lack; if broadband, the prolate coordinate does NOT make the object low-dimensional (scoped per supervisor: this falsifies the

evaluations.title: Where does the single-source peak live? Mass profile and peak-lag location of saved flat- vs peak-minimizers
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Test the mechanism behind the #502/#503 finding that bulk distance to flat is the wrong objective. Using the SAVED minimizers from Eval #502/#503 (no new optimization), characterize for each n and each minimizer type (L2-distance-min, Linf-distance-min, peak-min): the mass/boundary profile of the source w (is it edge-loaded?), the LOCATION of the autoconvolution peak lag (lag 0/end self-term, center cross-term, or interior?), and how concentrated the peak excess is across lags (participation ratio). Decides whether the bad peak of the bulk-flatness minimizer is a localized boundary/endpoint effect.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Phantom Pair-Sum Ecology of Zero-Gaps
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: To address Question #6 (Weighted Sumset Ecology), we test the hypothesis that zero-gaps act as corridors preventing the overpopulation of pair-sum bands at active lags. We load existing sparse artifacts (Evals 469, 453, 490) and identify their macroscopic zero-gaps. For each gap, we create a 'phantom' component representing mass filling the gap, and compute its cross-convolution with the actual profile. By measuring the overlap between the phantom's contribution band and the profile's active peak lags, we quantitatively determine if the gaps are precisely positioned to shield the active lags from collision pressure.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Coarse-Grained Pair-Sum Incidence Model
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: To address Question #6 (Weighted Sumset Ecology), we test a coarse-grained support-component model. We take three sparse artifacts (Evals 469, 453, 490) and abstract their active support intervals into uniform blocks of equivalent total mass. We compute the autoconvolution of this coarse model to map the 'pair-sum incidence bands'. By analyzing the correlation between these coarse incidence bands and the true profile's active peak lags and zero-gaps, we quantitatively determine if a simplified additive-combinatorial ecology predicts macroscopic topology without requiring the full high-frequency continuous envelope.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Dense-Envelope Counterfactual Pressure Landscape
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if the locations of zero-gaps are predicted by the 'counterfactual pressure' of the underlying dense envelope. For three sparse SOTA artifacts (Evals 469, 484, 490), we reconstruct their continuous dense envelopes by applying a low-pass Gaussian filter to fill their exact zero-gaps. We then compute the autoconvolution of these dense envelopes. We hypothesize that the locations of the original exact zero-gaps overlap precisely with the highest-pressure active lags of the dense envelope's autoconvolution. If true, this provides a predictive, transferable invariant for gap formation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Mapping Fejér-Riesz Root Flips to Macroscopic Spatial Gaps (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Investigates the mapping between discrete root configurations in the Fejér-Riesz orbit and the resulting macroscopic spatial envelopes by systematically flipping angular sectors of roots of the uniform vector.

evaluations.title: Exact algebraic structure of the small-n single-source minimax optimum and its KKT multiplier measure
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Probe whether the single-source low-peak minimax optimum w*(n) and its KKT dual-measure mu*(n) (Archive #6 stationarity object) have EXACT algebraic structure at small n, beyond the known closed forms R*(2)~(2,1), R*(3)~(8,4,3). For n up to ~14, solve the minimax to very high precision, extract w*, the active argmax-lag set, and the multiplier measure mu* satisfying back-convolution flatness on supp(w); then test for closed-form/minimal-polynomial structure in w*, recurrences or laws in the active-lag positions and |supp mu*|, the weights of mu*, and any algebraic relation between mu*'s support and the spectral zeros of w*(z). Predeclared decision rule on whether a closed-form

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Phantom Pressure Prediction of Gap Stability
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if the 'phantom pressure' model can predict gap stability *before* spatial optimization. We take the dense cap-form envelope. We test true stable gaps against false arbitrary gaps of the same width. For each gap, we create a phantom mass filling it, and compute its cross-convolution with the dense envelope. The hypothesis: phantom mass in true gaps creates massive, insurmountable new pressure peaks (predicting the gap *must* exist), while phantom mass in false gaps creates smaller, manageable peaks (predicting the gap is arbitrary and will refill during optimization).

evaluations.title: Phase-Space Trajectory Diagnostic: Root Migration at N=64
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We map the continuous spatial descent of our sparsification pipeline into the discrete Fejér-Riesz orbit. We optimize a dense cap-form envelope at N=64 until exact zero-gaps form. We then extract all 63 complex roots of both the initial dense polynomial and the final sparse polynomial. By pairing the roots, we identify exactly which conjugate pairs migrated across the unit circle, deterministically inducing the spatial zero-gaps. This provides a direct structural mapping between phase-root flips and spatial topology.

evaluations.title: Split-source cross-shadow closure audit
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score analysis testing whether degree-6 source-free closure changes carry residual information for near-flat one-source objects after deterministic source splits, or whether they reduce to lower-order omitted cross-shadow proxies.

evaluations.title: Exact fusion penalty: collapsing the two-source flat object into one source, R(W+reversal W) = n(1+2||W||^2)/(2n-1)
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Formalize Noether's fusion-penalty question using Archive #23 as the exactly-solvable test object. For the two-source flat decomposition W^2+reversal(W)^2=P_N, fusing into one source u=W+reversal(W) gives u*u = flat + 2(W*reversal(W)), a forced CENTER cross-term spike (Cauchy-Schwarz, peak at center lag = ||W||^2). I derive the exact fused peak R(u)=n(1+2||W||^2)/(2n-1) and need its asymptotics in n via ||W||_2^2 for the q-binomial closed form. The experiment confirms the exact formula and extracts the large-n constant, and validates that the Eval #508 L2-distance minimizer is approximated by a two-lump split whose cross-term predicts its center spike.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Combinatorial Mapping of Fejér-Riesz Root-Flips to Spatial Topology (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a 1,000-seed Monte Carlo exploration of the discrete root-flip space at N=64, mapping binary conjugate root selections to macroscopic Quarter Mass splits and spatial zero-gaps to address Question #7.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Large-Scale Predictive Invariant Test (N=64 to N=2048)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the predictive power of the dense active-lag count invariant on 50 distinct N=64 topologies, lifting them to N=2048 to measure whether their dense geometry predicts their sparse condensation efficiency.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Ecological Sensitivity (Mass-Matched Phantom Pressure)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Refining the phantom pressure model from Eval 514. To predict gap locations, we must control for base mass. We take a dense cap-form envelope and inject exactly the same small unit mass into 10 intervals corresponding to true sparse zero-gaps, and 10 'false' intervals. We measure the resulting pressure peak delta for each. We hypothesize that true gap locations possess structurally higher 'ecological sensitivity' (higher pressure delta per unit mass added) because their pair-sum incidence bands directly align with fragile high-pressure plateaus.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Out-of-Sample Root Flip Gap Prediction
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if specific, localized discrete root-flips deterministically predict macroscopic changes to spatial zero-gaps, without any spatial optimization. We take the sparse cap-form SOTA (N=128 for tractable root extraction), extract its roots, and manually flip one specific conjugate pair of roots across the unit circle. We reconstruct the spatial sequence and evaluate the immediate out-of-sample impact on the largest zero-gap. This tests if discrete phase-space navigation provides a coherent coordinate system for macroscopic support topology.

evaluations.title: Near-flat stability curve and the energy growth of the two-square source: does bounded bulk distance force peak excess?
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Two load-bearing results to elevate the center-cross-term paper. (A) Analytic/high-precision determination of the growth law of ||W||_2^2 for the Archive #23 q-binomial source, making the exact fusion penalty R(u)=n(1+2||W||_2^2)/(2n-1) rigorously scaling (test c0+c1*log n and a closed form). (B) An empirical near-flat stability curve: for several n and a sweep of bulk-distance budgets epsilon, measure the minimum achievable single-source normalized peak (and center-lag value) subject to ||normalize(h*h)-flat||_2 <= epsilon. Predeclared decision: does the minimum peak excess vanish as epsilon->0 or stay bounded below at fixed n (an empirical near-flat stability obstruction)?

evaluations.title: f-variable Lasserre level-2 certified lower bound on the autoconvolution peak (n=5,6): is perfect-square structure visible at degree 4?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: A bounded, decisive diagnostic. Compute a certified lower bound on min over nonnegative weights of the equal-grid autoconvolution peak R(w)=2n*max(conv(w,w))/(sum w)^2, using the Lasserre moment-SOS hierarchy at level 2 (degree-4 moments) DIRECTLY in the weight variables w (the square-root variables), at n=5 and n=6. The question is binary: does the level-2 certified lower bound exceed the certified energy floor 1.1478066521, or not? This tests whether the perfect-square/nonnegativity structure becomes visible to a moment-SOS relaxation at the lowest nontrivial order. Distinct from prior g-variable/power-sum SOS (which relaxes toward the moment class and can be saturated by a two-level box that has

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Deterministic Root-Group Gap Induction (N=64)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if specific groups of root flips deterministically induce macroscopic spatial zero-gaps. We take the dense cap-form base from Eval 515 (N=64) and the sparse cap-form from Eval 515. We extract the roots of both. We manually flip the specific subset of roots in the dense polynomial that correspond to the unit-circle crossings observed in the sparse polynomial. We reconstruct the spatial sequence directly from these flipped roots to see if it natively exhibits the zero-gap topology, without any continuous spatial optimization.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Out-of-Sample Predictive Invariant Test (N=64 to N=4096)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Replicates the 50-branch predictive invariant test (Eval #519) at a higher resolution (N=4096) to determine if the observed correlations between dense continuous score and final sparse score are robust to scale.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Sparse Inheritance
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Computes 1000-resample bootstrap confidence intervals for the Pearson and Spearman correlations derived in the 50-branch scale-flow populations (Eval #519).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Root-Interleaving of the Cyclotomic Ideal
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if discrete root interleaving can construct a novel sparse topology that bypasses the single-source cross-term penalty. We generate the roots of Phoenix II's cyclotomic components W and reversal(W) at N=64. We construct a single polynomial by interleaving their roots (e.g., alternating one root from W, one from reversal(W) sorted by angle). We reconstruct the spatial sequence and evaluate its topology and score to see if it suppresses the central peak observed in linear fusion.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Cross-Branch Ecological Sensitivity Atlas
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if mass-normalized phantom pressure (Ecological Sensitivity) is a universal, transferable invariant that predicts zero-gap locations across completely distinct topological branches. We generate the continuous 'Sensitivity Landscape' for three distinct SOTA objects (Cap-form, Axiom Branch, Melting Dirac Combs) by injecting a unit mass at every spatial coordinate individually and computing the marginal pressure delta. We test if the actual zero-gaps formed by spatial optimization perfectly align with the absolute maxima of this continuous sensitivity landscape, completely independently of the branch's specific macroscopic shape.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Forward Prediction of Zero-Gaps via PMTI
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: We test if the Pressure/Mass Tradeoff Index (PMTI) can perfectly forward-predict the location of spatial zero-gaps purely from the dense envelope, without any prior knowledge of the sparse mask. We compute the PMTI (Ecological Sensitivity divided by Dense Mass) across the dense cap-form envelope at N=1024. We identify the top 5 continuous intervals with the highest PMTI scores. We then compare these purely predicted intervals against the actual macroscopic zero-gaps that form during spatial sparsification.

evaluations.title: Minimal source-count of the flat self-convolution: exact Gram-rank certifier across supports
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the minimal number r*(S) of real squares needed to represent the flat (all-ones) self-convolution target on the sumset S+S, with each square supported on S, is governed by boundary geometry. Pencil work (this session) proved r*=2 for two length-2 intervals {0,1,3,4} via an explicit factorization P_8 = f1^2+f2^2, identical to the single interval, refuting a naive "more boundary components => larger r*" hypothesis. This evaluation builds an exact/certified Gram-rank certifier to compute r*(S) across a family of 1D supports (single interval, two and three intervals, varied lengths and gaps) and a 2D box/L-shape, recovering anchors (cycle r*=1, interval

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Active-Set Sparse Condensation and Topological Crossover Test
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether discrete active-set mask mutation can break the strict topological inheritance observed under continuous descent, evaluating if initially inferior dense branches can overtake superior branches via forced gap placement.

evaluations.title: Isolated-Sidon lower bound for flat source-count: is r*(S) the pinned-clique number, and is it a multiplicity-multiset invariant?
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests two predeclared questions about the minimal source-count r*(S) of the flat self-convolution (min rank of a symmetric PSD Gram indexed by S with all lag sums prescribed to 1). A proven lower bound (this session): r*(S) >= iota(S), where iota(S) is the largest "isolated Sidon subset" size — a subset T whose every within-T pair-sum is a globally unique lag in S+S, forcing the principal submatrix M[T,T]=(1/2)(I+J_|T|) of full rank |T|. iota is tight at both known extremes (Sidon iota=|S|; interval/box iota=2). The experiment computes the multiplicity multiset {r_S(k)}, iota(S), and exact r*(S) across 1D supports of size 2..7

evaluations.title: D2 multiplier lead: does a fixed perturbed multiplier m=1+εφ raise the inner energy-min above the floor? (same-n differential test, non-confounded)
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: A decisive differential diagnostic for a lower-bound lead, NOT a score run and NOT a standalone certificate. For the peak device max(conv(w,w))-based functional, define Phi(m)=inf over nonnegative unit-sum w of (sum_k m_k (w*w)_k^2)/(sum_k m_k (w*w)_k). Phi(1) is the energy floor. The lead: perturbing the multiplier m away from uniform in the direction phi = g*(g*-E0) (g* the energy minimizer, E0 its energy) has positive first variation, so sup_m Phi(m) may exceed the floor — the first resolution-free above-floor multiplier bound, contingent on energy-minimizer uniqueness/non-degeneracy. Test it numerically by a SAME-n comparison Phi_n(1+eps*phi) vs Phi_n(1), where resolution drift cancels and the

evaluations.title: Fixed-multiplier resolution test for D2: does ONE fixed m0 keep the dual above the energy floor as n grows? (the resolution-free claim #533 did not test)
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Decisive diagnostic for whether the quadratic multiplier dual is resolution-free, NOT a score run. For a SINGLE fixed nonnegative multiplier m0 on the autoconvolution support, the device gives R*_n >= inf_w (sum_k m0_k (w*w)_k^2)/(sum_k m0_k (w*w)_k). Eval #533 confirmed a per-n improvement but used an n-dependent perturbation, so it did not test resolution-freeness. Here we fix m0 once (from the n=40 energy-minimizer direction) and ask whether the device's R-scale value stays strictly above the energy floor 1.1478 uniformly as n grows (20,40,80,160), or decays to the floor. The inner multistart MINIMIZATION is conservative for the beats-floor claim: it actively searches

evaluations.title: Energy-minimizer rigidity for the D2 phase gap: distinct-minimizer count, Hessian nullity, and the residual sign condition ∫cos·ψ
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: The first-variation analysis of the D2 multiplier dual reduces the question "does a fixed multiplier push the dual strictly above the energy floor E0=1.1478?" to a structural property of the energy-minimizer set M: D2>E0 (to first order) iff 0 is not in conv{psi_{g*}: g* in M}, where psi_{g*}=g*^2 - E0*g* (mean-zero). For a single minimizer this is unconditional (psi=0 would force a two-level box, which is not an autoconvolution). This diagnostic maps the actual structure of M at several resolutions: how many distinct minimizers (mod reflection) achieve the floor, whether the energy Hessian has near-zero modes beyond the trivial scaling/reflection

evaluations.title: Phase-Root Transition Operator: Controlled L2 Shock Test (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a discrete radial root flip acts as a structured topological transition operator or merely a random spatial shock. Compares the re-equilibrated landing branch of a single root-flip against a random noise shock of exactly matched L2 magnitude.

evaluations.title: Verification of the bispectral lag-multiplier identity: exactness, the magnitude/phase split, and sign-indefiniteness of the phase term
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Numerically verifies the exact discrete identity Sum_j mu_j c_j^2 = (1/N^2) Sum_{p,q} hatw_p^2 hatw_q^2 tildemu(p+q), where c=w*w and hatc_p=hatw_p^2, decomposed into a magnitude-only term (conjugate pairing p+q=0, giving Sum |hatw_p|^4 — the Cohn-Elkies energy floor) plus a phase-bearing bispectral term (p+q!=0, nonzero iff mu is non-constant). Confirms exactness to roundoff across random nonnegative w, several n, and several lag-multipliers; confirms the magnitude-only collapse for constant mu; exhibits nonnegative w for which the p+q!=0 phase term is NEGATIVE (sign-indefinite), justifying that a PD/Bochner dual cannot certify the multiplier lift and that a w>=0 cone-positivity certificate is required. Also ties the first-variation

evaluations.title: Exploratory Transition: Sequential Ecological Masking (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests an ecologically informed discrete transition operator: sequentially hard-masking candidate spatial intervals based on their unit-mass phantom pressure, followed by active-set re-equilibration, to transition branches across topological valleys.

evaluations.title: Verification of strict convexity of ∫(f*f)² and a numerical estimate of D2=sup_{m>=0} Phi(m): how far above the energy floor does the multiplier dual reach?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract:
Verifies the strict-convexity theorem Q''(s)=8∫(f_s*h)^2+4∫(f_s*f_s)(h*h)=4∫|fhat_s|^2|hhat|^2
(2+cos2Δ)>=4∫|fhat_s|^2|hhat|^2>0 for the autoconvolution energy Q(f)=∫(f*f)^2, confirming the
energy minimizer is unique and even. Then numerically estimates D2=sup_{m>=0} Phi(m),
Phi(m)=inf_f ∫m g^2/∫m g, at fixed n by optimizing the multiplier m together with the inner
minimization, to locate D2 inside the proven interval (E0, R*]. NON-SCORE verification +
exploration; success = the convexity modulus inequality holds across random feasible directions,
the minimizer is even to tolerance, and a robust same-n estimate of D2 with its gap above the
floor is produced. Returns the safe incumbent for the official score field.

evaluations.title: Exploratory Transition: Sequential Ecological Masking on Cap-Form Branch (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the Sequential Ecological Masking operator on the dense Cap-form envelope at N=1024 to determine if phantom pair-sum pressure can sequentially carve the known stable SOTA gaps.

evaluations.title: Is high source-count confined to gappy supports? Contiguous-sumset vs r*, plus exact rank-3 witness for {0,1,2,5}
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a predeclared hypothesis bearing on whether the exact-flat source-count program (Archive #27) connects to the task's near-flat peak. The task requires the autoconvolution to be flat over a CONTIGUOUS lag interval, so any near-flat-relevant support S must have a contiguous sumset S+S (gaps are deviations). Hypothesis: source-count rigidity r*(S)>=3 occurs only when S+S has gaps (the task-irrelevant regime); contiguous-sumset supports have r*=2. Re-analyzes the existing Eval #532 scan (565 1D + small 2D supports) by cross-tabulating "S+S contiguous" against r*, and provides the exact rational rank-3 Gram witness for {0,1,2,5} requested by the Archive #27 review. Predeclared fork: no

evaluations.title: Exploratory Transition: Macroscopic Branch Splicing (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests branch splicing—combining the left half of one topological branch with the right half of another—as a constructive transition operator to generate novel macroscopic envelopes.

evaluations.title: Does sign freedom help autoconvolution flatness? delta_signed vs delta_nn on the interval (renewal bridge probe)
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the signed real sum-of-squares object underlying Archive #27 is a faithful proxy for the task's nonnegative single-source near-flat problem, or lives in a different (signed) regime. For the interval support S={0,...,n-1}, compares two minimal normalized autoconvolution distances-to-flat: delta_signed(n) over real v, and delta_nn(n) over v>=0 (the task object). Hand analysis at n=2,3 suggests sign freedom does NOT obviously help autoconvolution flatness (the all-positive flat target rigidly couples signs; lowering the center via opposite-sign endpoints breaks the side lags), unlike autocorrelation/merit-factor where signs dominate. Predeclared trichotomy: A) delta_signed ~ delta_nn (both floored) => signed object faithful proxy; B) delta_signed

evaluations.title: Sequential PMTI support-label forecast for Q6
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: A focused non-score model-organism audit for Question #6. It tests whether a predeclared sequential PMTI support-label process improves secondary sparse-gap forecasting over static PMTI after the primary cap-form gap is declared and removed.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Unconstrained Root-Space Optimization via Soft Non-Negativity Penalty
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the spatial sequence purely by its N-1 roots. Bypasses strict non-negative spatial bounds by using an unconstrained Adam optimizer on the roots, applying an annealed soft penalty for spatial negativity. This tests whether relaxing spatial hard bounds allows continuous escape from the 1.505 attractor.

evaluations.title: Simultaneous Soft-Penalty Hysteresis Test (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a simultaneous, static ecological penalty applied to a dense envelope can force it over a topological barrier, leading to a distinct unpenalized local minimum when the pressure is released.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Semidefinite Programming (SDP) Relaxation of Autoconvolution Peak
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the minimax autoconvolution problem as a convex Semidefinite Program (SDP) by relaxing the rank-1 constraint W = w w^T. Minimizes the maximum cross-diagonal sum of W >= 0, W >> 0. Evaluates the SDP at N=32, 64, 128, and uses the leading eigenvector of the optimal W* to initialize L-BFGS-B. This tests if the SDP global dual can provide a structural initialization to bypass the 1.505 spatial attractor.

evaluations.title: Simultaneous Soft-Penalty Control: Random Mask Hysteresis Test (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Acts as a negative control for Eval #546. Applies random static L1 penalties of equivalent magnitude to test whether hysteresis is an artifact of any large continuous deformation (optimizer path dependence) or specifically requires ecology-informed pair-sum pressure.

evaluations.title: Exact single-source near-flat autoconvolution delta on the interval at small n (active-set + PSLQ)
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract:
Computes the EXACT minimum single-source near-flat autoconvolution distance-to-flat on the
interval S={0,...,n-1} for small n, for both nonnegative and signed real sources:
delta_1(n) = min over v of ||v*v - c*1||_inf / c, c the mean lag. At n=2, Eval #543 found
0.4641016..., equal to the exact algebraic 2*sqrt(3)-3. This experiment seeks exact algebraic
values for n=2..6 via KKT/active-set + PSLQ recovery, to determine whether delta_1(n) has a
recognizable pattern/limit and whether the signed and nonnegative exact values coincide. A
predeclared theorem-or-bust probe; a bare list without provable structure is a non-publishable
outcome.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Combinatorial Phase Flipping via Root Reflection
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the Fejér-Riesz phase combinations. Generates a standard N=64 local minimum (score ~1.506). Computes its N-1 complex roots, groups them by conjugate pairs, and explores the 2^K discrete root reflections (z -> 1/z*) that perfectly preserve the autocorrelation magnitude. Searches for novel phase configurations with minimal spatial negativity, completely bypassing the 1.505 continuous spatial attractor.

evaluations.title: Corrected-normalization verification of the D2_n strict crossing: psi = c*^2 - a_n c*, derivative = 2n*sum psi^2, and the crossing margin across n
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Verifies the corrected finite-n multiplier-crossing identity behind Theorem 3 of the strict- convexity paper. With c* = w*_n * w*_n the discrete energy minimizer's autoconvolution, a_n = sum (c*)^2 (UNSCALED energy) and E0_n = 2n*a_n (scaled energy/floor), the admissible perturbation psi = c*^2 - a_n c* is mean-zero (sum psi = 0) and the one-sided derivative of Phi_n(1+eps*psi) equals 2n*sum psi^2 > 0, matching central finite differences. Confirms psi is not identically zero with a quantified margin (sum psi^2 and max|psi|) across n, and that the resulting Phi_n(1+eps*psi) strictly exceeds E0_n. NON-SCORE verification; success = exact match of analytic derivative

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Biquadratic Root-Space Descent from 1.506 Spatial Attractor
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the N=64 spatial sequence using 1 linear and 31 quadratic polynomial factors (63 real parameters). This explicitly guarantees a real spatial sequence while allowing complex roots to merge into real roots. Initializes the parameters precisely at the roots of the 1.506 spatial cap-form, then optimizes using JAX L-BFGS-B with a 1e7 soft-penalty on spatial negativity. This tests whether unconstrained spectral gradients can navigate around the active zero-bounds that trap continuous spatial descent.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extraction of N=32 Macroscopic Basins and Active Lags
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Setup run for the Monodromy lane. Runs a multi-start mapping at N=32 to reliably extract the Rank 1 and Cap-form branches, saving their normalized weights and identifying their exact sets of active autocorrelation lags.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Fienup Hybrid Input-Output (HIO) Phase Retrieval for Flat Spectrum
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Fienup HIO algorithm to find a non-negative spatial sequence whose autoconvolution perfectly matches a target flat 'boxcar' spectrum. Bypasses continuous spatial gradients completely. Bounces between the frequency domain (forcing target magnitudes) and the spatial domain (using HIO feedback to penalize negative values without hard clipping). Evaluates 100 random phase initializations to search for a new topological phase branch.

evaluations.title: Support-fullness of the autoconvolution energy minimizer: exhaustive small-n test of whether any gappy even support beats full support
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the support-fullness lemma needed to make Archive #28's finite-n crossing unconditional for all n: is the unique even energy minimizer of E_n(w)=2nΣ(w*w)^2 on the simplex always FULLY supported on {0,...,n-1}? For each n in {4,...,9} we exhaustively enumerate all reflection-symmetric (even) support patterns, solve the strictly convex energy minimization restricted to each support (unique per support), and compare the best gappy-support energy to the full-support energy. Also reports, at the full-support minimizer, the KKT/stationarity quantities G_k=(c*⋆w*)_k vs a_n=Σ(c*)^2 and the inward derivative 8n(G_k - a_n) for filling each lag, to confirm the variational mechanism (holes are fillable because their

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Closed-Loop Active Lag Memory (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a closed continuous deformation loop between the N=32 Rank 1 and Cap-form branches using target-complement mass penalties. Measures whether the initial active-lag sets re-emerge upon return, testing for topological memory versus generic path dependence.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Spectral Orthant Boundary Mapping via Homotopy Fienup HIO
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a homotopy of target magnitude spectra from a known valid spectrum (the uniform triangle, score 2.0) to an invalid ideal spectrum (the flat boxcar). We apply Fienup HIO along this interpolation parameter gamma. The goal is to track the phase branch as it deforms from the 2.0 basin toward the lower-bound theoretical limit, stopping exactly when the spatial non-negativity constraint mathematically breaks.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Closed-Loop Active Lag Memory (N=32, lambda=0.1)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the target-complement hysteresis loop at N=32 using a strong penalty (lambda=0.1) to ensure the intermediate states escape their initial topological basins before testing if the return loop recovers the original active-lag sets.

evaluations.title: Phase 6: High-Resolution Polishing of the Singular Baseline
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The 1.505 cap-form attractor dominates random or smoothed initializations. However, the exact continuous baseline f(x) = 1/sqrt(x) achieves pi/2 (1.57) entirely without oscillation, relying on a singularity. We initialize a high-resolution (N=4096) sequence with this singular asymmetric profile and apply L-BFGS-B. This tests whether a completely different topological branch—one rooted in singularity rather than equiripple oscillation—can bypass the 1.505 barrier.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Topological Degradation via Iterative Random Loops (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the Cap-form branch exhibits resilient topological memory under a sequence of random structural shocks (lambda=0.1), or if generic path dependence permanently scrambles the active-lag set.

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Finite Field Sequence Mapping (Legendre & m-sequences)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons continuous deformation in favor of algebraic combinatorics. Generates Legendre sequences (quadratic residues modulo prime p) and maximal-length shift-register sequences (m-sequences). These binary sequences have perfectly uniform circular autocorrelation. We map them to non-negative reals (via w_k = (s_k + 1) / 2) and evaluate their aperiodic autoconvolution, then apply local polishing. The goal is to determine if finite-field algebraic skeletons populate fundamentally different geometric basins than those found by random or continuous initializations.

evaluations.title: K2: additively irreducible r*=2 supports beyond the interval
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Search for additively irreducible, non-Sidon, non-product supports S in Z with source-count r*(S)=2 that are NOT affine images of an interval, to test whether the cyclotomic two-square mechanism (Archive #23) is the unique route to r*=2. Either a witness (mechanism not unique) or structural evidence that r*=2 forces interval/product factorization is decision-changing for Question #9 sub-problem K2.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Topological Rupture and Random Degradation Sweep (N=32)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps random sparse penalty strength (lambda from 0.1 to 2.0) on the Cap-form branch to identify the rupture boundary where active-lag memory is permanently broken. Tests whether the shattered state degrades into noise or transitions into a recognizable new branch.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: Global Optimization via Differential Evolution (DE)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 1.505 barrier is an artifact of local gradient-based optimizers (like L-BFGS-B) getting jammed in active-constraint corners. We apply Differential Evolution (DE), a global stochastic search algorithm, at N=64. DE mutates parameter vectors directly and is immune to gradient singularities, potentially allowing it to walk along the complex boundary of the positive orthant and discover lower-scoring asymmetric basins.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Topological Rupture Boundary Test (N=32, lambda=1.0)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Applies a massive random sparse penalty (lambda=1.0) to the Cap-form branch to force a permanent rupture of active-lag memory. Tests whether the ruptured state degrades into an arbitrary high-peak configuration or transitions to a structured basin.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Global Functional Optimization via Singular Polynomials
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the sequence as a continuous function f(x) = x^alpha * (1-x)^beta * P(x)^2, where P(x) is a polynomial of degree 31. This explicitly enforces non-negativity and allows for boundary singularities (alpha, beta < 0). By optimizing the 34 parameters (alpha, beta, and 32 polynomial coefficients) using global Differential Evolution, we completely bypass the 1024-dimensional spatial grid traps. This searches the entire space of continuous, possibly singular, probability densities for the true global minimum.

evaluations.title: K2 reformulation: r*=2 as a support-restricted sum-of-two-squares of the sumset indicator
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Test the reformulation r*(S)=2 <=> indicator polynomial of S+S equals U(x)^2+V(x)^2 with supp(U),supp(V) subset S. Verify the equivalence numerically, check the necessary condition F_S(x)>=0 on R, and for irreducible non-interval supports with r*>=3 classify whether the obstruction is positivity (F_S<0 somewhere) or support-restriction (F_S>=0 but no S-supported SOS root). Goal: distinguish the genuinely cyclotomic property of the interval (vacuous support constraint) from the incidence-theoretic support obstruction.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Boolean Support Mask Genetic Algorithm
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Decouples the combinatorial active-set problem from continuous optimization. Evolves a population of Boolean masks (length 64) representing the structural zeros of the sequence. For each mask, we optimize only the strictly positive weights using L-BFGS-B. This explicitly searches the complex boundary of the non-negative orthant without relying on local gradients to add/drop active constraints, potentially finding the hidden topological branch.

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Setup: Extraction of N=64 Macroscopic Basins and Active Lags
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Setup run for Phase 3 Scale Flow. Runs a multi-start mapping at N=64 to extract the Rank 1 and Cap-form branches, saving their normalized weights and exact active-lag sets to serve as coordinates for higher-resolution monodromy loops.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Scale Flow of Target-Complement Monodromy Loop (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the conservative topological memory mapped by structural loops at N=32 scales invariantly to N=64, or if higher-dimensional landscapes become inherently dissipative, permanently shattering active-lag recovery.

evaluations.title: K2 breakdown table: counts by support size, r*, positivity status from saved artifacts
evaluations.author: Phoenix II
evaluations.abstract: Aggregate the saved K2 scan artifacts (Eval #562, #567) into a compact table broken down by support size |S|, r*-value, positivity status (F_S>=0 vs F_S<0), and unclassified/infeasible rows, to support the revised Archive paper. No new search; pure re-aggregation of existing JSON with exact counts and a clean printed table.

evaluations.title: Magnitude-fiber impostor hierarchy: how much bispectral memory destroys low-peak phase-retrieval impostors
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract:
Constructive test of Question #10's H1/H2 dichotomy. Fix a near-optimal low-peak step function and
search its Fourier-MAGNITUDE fiber (nonnegative step functions with identical power spectrum) for the
member of LOWEST autoconvolution peak — a low-peak "impostor." Measure the magnitude-fiber peak gap
(target peak minus fiber-min peak), then progressively constrain low-order bispectral coefficients and
measure how the fiber-min peak rises. Identify which bispectral data is load-bearing and whether a
resolution-independent amount of it lifts the fiber-min above the energy floor E0. Positive object
(impostor construction + rigidity identification), not a barrier certificate.

evaluations.title: Exact magnitude-fiber search by spectral-factorization root reflections: do low-peak nonnegative impostors exist, and which bispectral data kills them?
evaluations.author: Apeiron II
evaluations.abstract:
Fixes the search defect in Eval #572. Instead of a penalty search that collapsed to the target anchor,
parametrize the Fourier-MAGNITUDE fiber EXACTLY via Fejer-Riesz spectral-factorization root reflections
(the zero-flip group): each root r of the polynomial W(z)=sum w_k z^k reflects to 1/conj(r), exactly
preserving |W| on the unit circle. Enumerate/sample reflection subsets, keep the NONNEGATIVE
coefficient vectors (the binding constraint), and find the lowest-peak member. This yields a TRUE
magnitude-fiber min over real nonnegative step functions. Then ask which low-order bispectral
coefficients separate the low-peak nonnegative impostors from the target. Positive constructive object.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Topological Degradation via Random Loops (N=64)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the exact random sparse degradation loop that failed to rupture the Cap-form basin at N=32 (Eval #560) is sufficient to permanently rupture the N=64 Cap-form basin, comparing scale-dependent basin volume.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 1: Energy Minimizer and its Antisymmetric Hessian Modes
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the unique even energy minimizer (minimizing E = int g^2) at N=256 and computes the constrained Hessian of the phase-sensitive cubic functional J = int g^3 / int g^2 at this anchor point. Identifies the primary antisymmetric unstable eigenvectors, establishing the tangent directions for the spontaneous symmetry-breaking bifurcation path toward the L_inf global minimum.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 2: Tracing the Heteroclinic Orbit of the Cubic Functional
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Traces the exact 1D unstable manifold (heteroclinic orbit) from the symmetric energy minimizer saddle point down to the local minimum of the cubic functional J. By following the gradient flow starting from a tiny perturbation along the antisymmetric unstable eigenvector, we map a continuous, mathematically rigid symmetry-breaking path. We evaluate the true L_inf peak score along this entire path to detect if it crosses the 1.505 barrier or nucleates structural zero-gaps.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 3: Exact Homotopy Continuation from Energy to L_inf
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact homotopy H(w, t) = (1-t)*E(w) + t*L_alpha(w), bridging the strictly convex energy minimizer (t=0) and the non-convex LogSumExp peak objective (t=1). Traces the global minimum as t increases. At a critical t_c, the symmetric global minimum must undergo a pitchfork bifurcation into asymmetric branches. We track the asymmetry metric and the exact peak score to detect whether this rigorous continuous path nucleates macroscopic zero-gaps or folds.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 4: Active-Set Continuation and Barrier Localization
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces standard L-BFGS-B homotopy with an explicit Active-Set Continuation scheme. By tracking the sequence of boundary collisions (where w_i hits 0), we test whether the stalling at 1.518 in Eval 577 is a mere artifact of the continuous optimizer jamming against the orthant boundary, or a genuine KKT deadlock where no valid active-set transition permits further descent. Maps the exact sequence of zero-gap nucleations as the symmetry-breaking path descends from the energy minimizer.

evaluations.title: Small Support Lift-Fiber Atlas
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic to test whether lag-level pair-sum signatures control source-level local liftability. The evaluation enumerates small binary supports, groups them by lag multiplicity signatures, computes fixed-support derivative and elementary transport cone diagnostics, and saves explicit same-shadow examples where source-level move geometry differs.

evaluations.title: Minimal Incidence Memory for Lift-Fiber Shadows
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #579. Tests whether compact source-accountable memories, such as active-lag vertex incidence and derivative-row overlap, separate the same weak lag-shadow groups that had different source-level lift diagnostics. The goal is to turn the toy false witnesses into a concrete controlled-forgetting ladder.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 5: Unconstrained Theta-Squared Homotopy
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates the hard orthant boundary artifacts that jammed previous continuation attempts. Reparameterizes the weights as w = theta^2, allowing unconstrained optimization over the real line. The vanishing gradient at theta=0 naturally stabilizes structural zero-gaps without requiring explicit active-set dropping or clipping. Re-traces the homotopy from the energy minimizer to the L_alpha peak objective using unconstrained L-BFGS-B to see if the bifurcation path smoothly reaches the 1.505 cap-form.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Step 6: Interior-Point Central Path Homotopy
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eliminates hard active-set collisions by tracking the Interior-Point Central Path. We augment the homotopy with a log-barrier penalty nu * sum(-log(w_i)). As t goes from 0 to 1, nu(t) decays to zero. This ensures the bifurcation path from the energy minimizer smoothly navigates the complex geometry of the positive orthant without irreversible constraint dropping or theta-squared saddle artifacts, testing if the mathematically pure central path connects to the 1.505 cap-form.

evaluations.title: Active Incidence Memory on Frontier Transport States
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the active-edge overlap memory from Eval #580 has any non-toy signal on stored dense frontier states and transport continuations. The evaluation computes scalable active-lag incidence summaries for Nexus/Noema transport states, compares them to active-gradient geometry and accepted-move history, and returns an inherited valid construction unchanged.

evaluations.title: Generative Sequential Masking via Dynamic PMTI (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: We test the conjecture that zero-gap topology is a sequential PMTI cascade. Instead of relying on passive global spatial optimization, we actively construct a topology step-by-step. At each step, we partially equilibrate the sequence with a strict positive floor (preventing passive gap formation), calculate the dynamic PMTI landscape, permanently mask a continuous interval around the new PMTI maximum, and repeat. We evaluate if this greedy generative process diverges from the SOTA cap-form and if it can discover a novel topological basin.
