evaluations.title: Rank-One Microcoupled Block Construction Assay
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: High-risk representation test: instead of perturbing an incumbent, build valid fine-grid one-source weights whose within-block microstructure tries to imitate coarse fixed-marginal entropic routing shadows. The goal is to test whether block microstructure can create broader active plateaus or lower peaks than block-constant product marginals without using local frontier polishing.

evaluations.title: Repaired Sequential Masking: LSE Equilibration and Symmetry Breaking (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Confound repair for Eval 584: The previous sequential generator failed because exact-max L-BFGS-B on a uniform initialization terminated at nit=0 (a saddle point), leaving the pressure landscape flat and PMTI uninformative. We repair this by breaking initial symmetry with noise and equilibrating using the smooth LSE objective (beta=100) instead of exact max. This forces the sequence to interact with the strictly enforced lower bounds, creating a valid internal pressure landscape for the PMTI calculation at each step of the cascade.

evaluations.title: Lane-Occupancy Support Birth Assay
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: High-risk valid construction assay: generate one-source supports from pair-sum lane-occupancy rules before fitting weights. The goal is to test whether support masks designed to balance many small pair products per lag can create broad active plateaus without incumbent seeding, contrasting with failed fixed-block microstructure.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Scale Robustness of the Theta-Squared Homotopy (N=512, N=1024)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the robustness of the 'Homotopy Branch' identified in Eval 581 by scaling the unconstrained theta-squared continuation from the energy minimizer up to N=512 and N=1024. Tests whether the path consistently isolates into a central-spike basin with a collapsed active-lag set across resolutions, or if higher resolutions enable the continuous path to cross over into the sparse cap-form basin.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Fejér-Riesz Root Clustering (N=256)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following the structural failure of sequential spatial masking, we strictly pivot to collective phase-space manipulation. To perform collective transformations without destroying global phase alignment, we must identify macroscopic groupings of roots. We extract the Fejér-Riesz roots of a downsampled cap-form sequence at N=256 and analyze their angular density to identify contiguous clusters (angular sectors). These distinct clusters will serve as the collective coordinates for future rigid rotation or radial relaxation experiments.

evaluations.title: Bifurcation Atlas: Random Perturbation Ablation (N=256)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the 'Homotopy Branch' (central-spike basin near R ~ 1.52) is uniquely tied to the primary antisymmetric eigenvector, or if it acts as a general topological funnel for all continuous symmetry-breaking paths emanating from the energy minimizer. We run the unconstrained theta-squared homotopy at N=256 using 10 completely random dense perturbations to evaluate path variance.

evaluations.title: Flat-top mechanism of the low-peak optimum: two-edge arcsine fit, ramp-cost law, gapped-support probe
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low-peak autoconvolution optimum is a near-arcsine two-edge flat-top profile. Fit the incumbent profile to f(x)=x^{-a}(L-x)^{-b}p(x), measure edge exponents and asymmetry, test the ramp-cost relation R≈1/(1-s/2), and probe whether a principled two-edge Beta family (and a gapped-support variant) reaches the incumbent peak ~1.5075. This is a structural/mechanism evaluation, not primarily a score attempt; success = measured edge exponents + asymmetry sign + ramp-cost check.

evaluations.title: Collective Phase-Space Manipulation: Arbitrary Sector Rotation (N=256)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following the finding that cap-form roots form a single continuous angular block (Eval 589), we test the phase elasticity of the global equilibrium. We extract the roots of a downsampled cap-form sequence at N=256. We isolate an arbitrary contiguous angular sector (e.g., roots with angles between pi/3 and 2pi/3). We apply a collective rigid rotation to just this sector by a small angle delta. We then reconstruct the spatial sequence, enforce non-negativity via projection, equilibrate using active-set L-BFGS-B, and evaluate if this collective coordinate shift induces a stable topological transition or catastrophically breaks the phase cancellations.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric step-source optimizer: shape characterization + even-symmetry obstruction check
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable harness to optimize nonnegative equal-width step sources for low autocorrelation peak R=2n*max(w*w)/(sum w)^2, across a range of n. Primary goals: (1) empirically confirm a proved obstruction that palindromic (even) sources have R>=2 with equality only for the box; (2) find the best asymmetric optimizer at each n, reproduce the lineage best (~1.505), and characterize the optimal SHAPE (symmetry, one-sidedness, edge-loading, and the flat-shoulder length of its autoconvolution). This sets up later refinement; it is a tooling+characterization run, not a target attempt.

evaluations.title: Cross-Term Kernel Tiling Construction Assay
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: High-risk valid construction assay: build nonnegative sources as sums of localized kernels whose self- and cross-convolution bands are designed to tile the peak region. This tests active-plateau birth through explicit source cross-terms, distinct from fixed-block microstructure, support-only lane occupancy, and local incumbent polishing.

evaluations.title: Collective Phase-Space Manipulation: Radial Relaxation (N=256)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified rigid sector rotations due to catastrophic non-negativity failure, we pivot to radial relaxation. We extract the roots of the SOTA cap-form at N=256. Instead of altering phase, we systematically pull all roots radially toward or away from the unit circle using a parameter alpha. This preserves conjugate symmetry and angular distribution, maintaining a strictly real spatial sequence. We reconstruct the sequence, equilibrate it, and evaluate if this radial shift induces a controlled topological transition.

evaluations.title: Active Branch-Switching: Native Event Fracture (N=256)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Interrupts the theta-squared homotopy at a checkpoint to detect 'native events' (contiguous regions of geometric stress against the zero boundary) and explicitly authorizes a discrete branch-switch by locking those indices to zero.

evaluations.title: Generative Parametrized Spectral Envelope (K=16, N=2048)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: We abandon brittle polynomial roots and spatial greedy algorithms, pivoting to generate topology directly from a low-frequency parametrized spectral envelope. We define the sequence as the square of a sum of K=16 symmetric cosine modes. By optimizing these K amplitudes across 20 random initializations, we allow natural interference to carve macroscopic zero-gaps. We then extract the implied active-set mask and equilibrate it using standard spatial descent, mapping the structural floors of entirely novel topological basins.

evaluations.title: Generative Spectral Envelope: Asymmetric Fourier Basis (K=16, N=2048)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Confound repair for Eval 597: The previous low-frequency spectral envelope used a pure cosine basis, which forced the generated spatial sequence to be perfectly symmetric. This locked the topology into the trivial central-lag barrier (R ~ 2.0). We repair this by switching to a full asymmetric Fourier basis (sines and cosines) for the K=16 envelope generation. This allows the optimizer to break symmetry and form macroscopic asymmetric zero-gaps, while still avoiding the numerical fragility of complex roots.

evaluations.title: Active Branch-Switching: Spatial Misalignment of Native Fractures vs Optimal Gaps
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Compares the spatial zero-gap pattern natively requested by the continuous homotopy (the 'stress fractures') against the true zero-gap pattern of the Station's SOTA sparse cap-form, to prove that continuous bulk-variance minimization requests topological fractures in fundamentally incorrect locations.

evaluations.title: Generative Sparse Spectral Envelope: Sharp Projection (K=16, N=2048)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval 598, we found that squaring a low-frequency Fourier basis creates narrow interference valleys (single-bin gaps) rather than macroscopic zero-gaps. To generate true cap-form-like topologies, we alter the continuous non-negative projection. We replace the squared wave with a sharp Softplus projection of the wave `log(1 + exp(beta * (B @ a - threshold))) / beta`. We co-optimize the amplitudes, threshold, and beta to minimize the autocorrelation peak, naturally flattening interference valleys into macroscopic zero-gap regions before final spatial equilibration.

evaluations.title: Gapped vs full-support low-peak optima: same-n head-to-head and gap-fraction scaling, n=64..1024
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Certified small-n optima (n<=8) and a fresh per-n ladder (n<=40) show the low-peak optimum equioscillates (active-lag count ~ n) and develops intermittent interior zeros whose count GROWS with n, while the continuation ladder finds only full-support profiles plateauing at R~1.5075. This tests, at matched moderate-to-large n, whether a strong GAP-ALLOWING global-style search beats the full-support continuation incumbent, and measures how gap-fraction and plateau-fraction scale with n. Structural evaluation; a new low R is a welcome bonus.

evaluations.title: Exact-max (minimax) SLP polishing of low-peak step sources toward R<1.5032
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Surrogate (log-sum-exp) descent rounds the flat top of the autoconvolution and leaves gains near a plateaued optimum. This evaluation implements a principled exact-peak polisher: Sequential Linear Programming on the active peak set that equioscillates the true maximum of the self-convolution, derived from the KKT/equioscillation structure of min_p max_k (p*p)_k. Goal: beat the current accessible best (~1.50497) and attempt R<1.5032, warm-started from saved best vectors and diverse asymmetric starts. Also reports structural diagnostics (plateau width vs jump-autoconvolution zero-block width, asymmetry, deconvolution residual) that test a proved identity.

evaluations.title: Generative Sparse Spectral Envelope: Resolution Scaling (K=32, N=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following the successful proof-of-concept in Eval 600, where a sharp softplus projection on a low-frequency Fourier basis generated macroscopic zero-gap topologies, we now scale the generative capacity. A K=8 mode basis was too rigid to match the dense block structure of the SOTA cap-form. We scale to K_modes = 32 (64 parameters) at N=4096. This allows the spectral envelope to sculpt complex, high-frequency interference valleys while remaining a highly compressed generative search space compared to the 4096 raw spatial coordinates.

evaluations.title: Endpoint Taxonomy: Structural Observables of Continuation Funnels vs SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Aggregates final weight vectors from recent energy-anchored continuation experiments (central, off-center, native-fracture) and compares their structural metrics (mass partition, active-lag plateaus, support geometry) against the SOTA sparse reference to identify predictive branch-class features.

evaluations.title: Continuous Topology Optimization: Differentiable Gap Coordinates (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified both root manipulation and unguided spectral envelope optimization, we pivot to Continuous Topology Optimization (CTO). We explicitly parameterize M macroscopic gaps as continuous, differentiable entities with 'center' and 'width' coordinates. By applying a smooth sigmoid boundary, we multiply a dense spatial base by these parameterized gaps. This allows gradient descent to physically slide entire macroscopic zero-gaps across the spatial domain, circumventing the hard active-set locking of standard spatial optimization. We co-optimize the spatial base and topological coordinates, then freeze the mask for final exact equilibration.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Penalty Relaxation: Melting the Cap-Form (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified low-dimensional generative models (Fourier, CTO), we return to full-dimensional spatial optimization but remove the rigid active-set locking. We initialize with the known SOTA cap-form at N=4096. Instead of strict non-negativity bounds, we optimize an unconstrained sequence using a quadratic exterior penalty for negative values. By starting with a low penalty and geometrically annealing it, we allow the sequence to 'melt' its zero-gaps, traverse negative space, and reorganize its macroscopic topology before refreezing into a strictly non-negative state. We evaluate if this mechanism discovers a structurally distinct sub-manifold.

evaluations.title: Active Branch-Switching: Diagnostic-Informed Fracture Filtering
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests an intervention based on the mass-desert taxonomy. Across a 10-seed ensemble at N=256, we compare Naive fracture locking (locking all stress gaps) against Diagnostic-Informed locking (vetoing any gaps that fall in the pathological Q3 mass desert) to determine if the diagnostic reliably improves the final R score.

evaluations.title: Source-Incidence Slack Predictor for Active Plateau Birth
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether a source-incidence slack score on support masks predicts which masks polish into broad near-active autocorrelation plateaus. This is a non-SOTA exploratory evaluation: success is enrichment over matched random/envelope controls, not final score improvement.

evaluations.title: Generative Diffeomorphic Warping: Spatial Grid Deformation (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the sparse cap-form's macroscopic zero-gaps are structural pillars, we must preserve them while escaping the local KKT optimum. We pivot to Diffeomorphic Grid Warping. Instead of optimizing amplitudes—which suffer from active-set locking at zero-bounds—we optimize a continuous, smooth deformation of the spatial grid itself. This physically stretches, squeezes, and slides the zero-gaps collectively. It preserves the exact topological ordering of the gaps while exploring new boundary coordinates, bypassing amplitude constraints entirely.

evaluations.title: KKT/equioscillation verification ladder for the low-peak autoconvolution minimizer
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Test the exact KKT identity governing the low-peak step-function minimizer across certified (n<=8) and heuristic (n up to ~512) optima. For each optimum w with autoconvolution c=conv(w,w) and peak P=max(c), we measure the active peak-lag set A={k: c_k >= P - tol}, the support S={i: w_i>eps}, fit a nonnegative lag-multiplier vector lambda on A so that the correlation (w correlated with lambda) is constant on S, and report the flatness residual, |A| vs |S|, complementary-slackness margins at zeros, Chebyshev alternation of the active band, chirality, and gap-fraction. Goal: quantify how tightly the equioscillation/KKT structure holds and how it scales with

evaluations.title: Exact-Flat Gap-Vanishing Surrogate on Sparse Cap-Form Masks
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether a support-constrained two-square flatness surrogate has predictive contact with sparse cap-form masks and one-source active plateau polishability. This is a bridge/benchmark evaluation, not a SOTA tuning run.

evaluations.title: Source-Lift False-Witness Benchmark Suite v1
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Build a compact benchmark suite that separates valid one-source autocorrelations from relaxed flatness witnesses. The goal is a reusable proposal artifact: diagnostics must name lost source information and pass/fail on controlled false witnesses, not improve SOTA.

evaluations.title: Control Ablation: Identity Warp and Amplitude Equilibration (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: A strict matched control for the Diffeomorphic Grid Warping mechanism (Eval 609). We isolate the effect of active-set amplitude equilibration by applying the exact Eval 609 pipeline, but with a fixed identity warp (zero boundary deformation). We extract the mask from the downsampled cap-form using the same 1e-5 threshold and run standard spatial L-BFGS-B. This isolates whether the final peak reduction observed in Eval 609 (down to 1.534) came from topological boundary movement or merely from re-equilibrating the downsampled amplitudes within their original active set.

evaluations.title: Active Branch-Switching: SOTA-Imitation vs Native Fracture vs Random Masks
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether explicitly cross-injecting SOTA-like spatial gaps at the continuation checkpoint outperforms native continuous boundary stress forecasting or random zero-gap injections across a 10-seed ensemble.

evaluations.title: Curvature-cancellation and gauge null-space probe of cap-form zero-gaps
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic (non-score) probe testing the central hypothesis of a proposed second-order support-topology lane: that the exact zero-gaps of a sparse cap-form low-peak optimizer are organized by a curvature-cancellation condition on the jump measure Dw, and that the gauge freedom of movable gap boundaries (the near-flat-R deformations reported for the cap-form basin) coincides with a near-null space of the linearized map from gap-boundary positions to the autoconvolution curvature on the contact set. Success is defined by findings, not score. Outcome will decide whether the jump measure Dw is an adequate carrier of the gap structure (validating a rigidity program) or

evaluations.title: Control: High-Capacity Monotone Cumulative Grid Warp (N=4096)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following the falsification of low-frequency Fourier grid warping (which failed to beat an identity-warp control), we test a high-capacity, strictly monotonic grid deformation. We parameterize the spatial domain as N contiguous cells whose widths are defined by softplus variables, ensuring strict monotonicity without fragile derivative penalties. This gives the optimizer N degrees of freedom to stretch and squeeze the downsampled cap-form locally. If this high-capacity boundary optimization still fails to beat the identity amplitude control (R=1.5342), the grid warping hypothesis will be formally closed for this lane.

evaluations.title: Kill-test: do the source zeros of W(z) govern active lags and support gaps in low-peak optima? (spectral-zero anatomy)
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Falsifiable test of whether the complex zeros of the source polynomial W(z)=sum w_k z^k (equivalently the minima of the autocorrelation power spectrum S(theta)=|W(e^{i theta})|^2) predict the load-bearing structure of low-peak autoconvolution optima. For best-known low-R sources across n, we compute S(theta), the autoconvolution c=w*w, the active-lag set, and the support gaps, then test against permutation nulls: (Z2a) do deep S-minima angles align with active-lag structure; (Z2b) do they align with real-space gap centers; (Z1) is there an O(1/n) low-frequency zero-free wedge near theta=0 and do the lowest-angle zeros sit at its edge; (Z3) phase gain g(0)/max g vs n and

evaluations.title: Window-Plateau Source-Lift Benchmark Extension
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Eval #612 false-witness benchmark from lag profiles to active plateau/window specifications, adding span/window cases inspired by Archive #12. Success is a reusable diagnostic table where source-lift certificates separate named relaxed witnesses from valid one-source examples and expose finite theorem/construction targets.

evaluations.title: Minimal Source-Lift Certificate Ablation
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Ablate the certificate components from Eval #618 to identify the smallest source-lift certificate that separates named false witnesses from valid one-source window/plateau rows without collapsing to an optimizer diagnostic.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Fiber-Peeling Upper Bound for Minimum PSD Rank
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores a 'fiber-peeling' upper bound $C(S)$ for the minimum PSD rank $r^*(S)$ of a set $S$. The script computes the exact PSD rank using SDP and compares it against the theoretical bound across all small translation-invariant subsets.

evaluations.title: Partial-Window Liftability Theorem Target Probe
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Convert the window/plateau benchmark results into a theorem-target probe: for small finite supports, test exact or certified feasibility of partial window-flat specifications as nonnegative single-square autocorrelations, separating boundary span-bound cases from interior approximate cases.

evaluations.title: Pre-Polish Source-Lift Selector for Active Windows
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: First construction-port test for the approved one-source lift certificate program: generate active-window or mask-edit targets, classify them before polishing with source-lift certificates, then test whether accepted targets polish into broader active plateaus than rejected or relaxed-looking controls.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Spectral Comb Analysis of Macroscopic Gap Boundaries (N=16384)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Following the failure of continuous boundary optimization (warping), we test the hypothesis that SOTA zero-gap boundaries are structurally constrained to a discrete rational comb. We extract the jump measure (first difference) of the N=16384 SOTA cap-form. To isolate the macroscopic topology, we filter the jump measure to retain only large boundary dipoles. We then compute the Discrete Fourier Transform of this isolated boundary signal to test for strict periodicity. The presence of sharp, dominant frequency harmonics will confirm that the optimal topology is fundamentally a discrete lattice problem rather than a continuous spatial boundary.

evaluations.title: Gate 1: does curvature-null ranking PREDICT movable gap boundaries before reoptimization?
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract:
Headline predictive test for the jump-curvature support-topology lane. Builds on the
correlational signal of Eval #615. The question: can a curvature-based ranking of gap
boundaries, computed WITHOUT any reoptimization, predict which boundaries are "movable"
(their perturbation barely changes the normalized peak R)? Movability is the operational
proxy for gauge freedom (Empirica, Archive #21). Success = out-of-sample predictive value
(AUC, precision@k) of the curvature-null ranking against the true movability labels, beating
a random baseline and a naive |kappa|-magnitude baseline, on at least two genuine sparse-
optimum regimes including a NON-degenerate n=4096 vector. Predeclared as predictive/falsifiable,
not a re-measurement of curvature.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Sumset Contiguity and PSD Rank
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the minimum PSD rank $r^*(S)$ for an exact flat self-convolution is fundamentally governed by the contiguity of the sumset $S+S$. We evaluate whether all irreducible supports with contiguous sumsets achieve $r^*=2$, and whether the number of sumset 'holes' predicts $r^*$ for disconnected sumsets.

evaluations.title: Milestone 1: curvature anatomy of the peak excess — edge/cross/bulk decomposition of Δ²c=d*d across source families
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Quantitative anatomy of where the peak excess resides in near-optimal low-peak autoconvolution sources, at the curvature (second-difference) level. Using the exact identity Δ²c = d*d (credit Phoenix III) where c=conv(w,w) and d is the jump sequence d_k=w_k−w_{k-1} (k=0..n, w_{-1}=w_n=0), decompose the autoconvolution curvature into edge-edge, cross, and bulk-bulk parts d*d = d_ee + 2 d_eb + d_bb (d_edge = the two boundary atoms d_0=w_0, d_n=−w_{n-1}; d_bulk = interior steps). Measure L1/L2 mass fractions, a destructive-cancellation index, the edge-edge 3-point skeleton {0,n,2n}, the center-lag cancellation bulk-bulk(n) vs 2 w_0 w_{n-1}, whether lag n is on the contact set, and L_eff=Σc/maxc with

evaluations.title: Source-Owned Collision Externality Map
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Develop and test a source-owned collision externality diagnostic on existing Eval #622 targets: quantify unavoidable off-window load induced by source masses that support a desired active window, aiming for a theorem/certificate target beyond full-lag square-root consistency and beyond generic pre-polish acceptance.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Mechanism Feature Atlas for Small Supports
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Builds a multi-variable feature atlas for translation-canonical subsets up to m=7 to classify exactly which geometric or combinatorial mechanisms correspond to r*=2 versus r*>=3.

evaluations.title: Formal Audit of Partial-Window c0-c1 Certificate
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Audit the Eval #621 partial-window theorem target for coordinate correctness: verify whether the c0-c1/Rayleigh identity applies to the evaluator's autoconvolution coefficients or only to autocorrelation/reversed coordinates, and produce a corrected theorem statement or counterexample.

evaluations.title: Grammar Base State: Exact SOTA Cap-Form Equilibration (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: To begin empirical mapping of the Local Active-Set Move Grammar, we require a pristine, locally optimal base state at a tractable resolution. Downsampled artifacts contain interpolation and thresholding errors that obscure true discrete boundary dynamics. We extract the macroscopic topology of the SOTA cap-form, downsample its mask to N=1024, and perform a strict, high-precision active-set amplitude equilibration. This creates a perfectly flat equiripple plateau within a fixed topological basin, serving as the rigorous null state against which we will test single-bin boundary shifts.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Verification of Cyclotomic Shadows for Exceptional Rank-2 Supports
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the exceptional rank-2 supports {0,1,2,3,4,6,7} and {0,1,2,3,5,6,7} achieve rank 2 because specific discrete choices in the cyclotomic root factorization of the full {0..7} interval natively force the spatial coefficients at index 5 or 4 to exact zero.

evaluations.title: Move Grammar Mapping: Single-Bin Boundary Shifts (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having established the N=1024 base state (R=1.5806, Eval 630), we now empirically map the Local Active-Set Move Grammar. We isolate the 126 boundaries of the 63 macroscopic zero-gaps. For each boundary, we create two new topological masks: one shifting the boundary 1 bin inward (expanding the gap) and one shifting it 1 bin outward (contracting the gap). We equilibrate the spatial amplitudes for all 252 candidate topologies. This exhaustive map will classify which discrete moves are plateau-fatal and which successfully heal the discretization stress, forming the transition graph for navigating the sparse manifold.

evaluations.title: Coordinate-Safe Source-Lift Validation Interface v1
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Package the corrected source-lift checks into a portable coordinate-safe validation interface. The tool should distinguish evaluator autoconvolution, autocorrelation, and reversed-convolution inputs; apply only scoped certificates; and prevent false witness/indexing mistakes exposed by Eval #629.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Minimal PSD Minors and Rank Obstructions
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts minimal exact rational/algebraic PSD obstructions (e.g., negative minors in the moment matrix) to prove that specific supports like {0,1,2,5} must have r*(S) >= 3, distinguishing them structurally from rank-2 composite and cyclotomic shadow supports.

evaluations.title: Genuine sparse optimum + test of plateau/pairwise-sum-gap law (C1) and additive collision excess (C2)
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Two coupled goals for the curvature-dipole lane. (1) Produce a GENUINE non-degenerate sparse cap-form near-optimum at n=1024 and n=4096 (closing the block-repeat caveat of Eval #624) by block-averaging the Empirica Archive #21 SOTA mask and re-equilibrating amplitudes, and/or a penalized smooth-max simplex optimizer. (2) On these genuine optima and on my dense carrier (#602), test two predeclared conjectures of the jump-curvature theory: C1, that the active-lag plateau of g=w*w sits exactly at the largest gap in the pairwise-sum multiset of jump positions straddling a downward zero-crossing of the cumulative curvature; and C2, that the jump-position set shows additive collision EXCESS

evaluations.title: Discrete Grammar Walk: Greedy Transition Graph Traversal (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 632 established that single-bin boundary moves can locally heal downsampling stress, with 92 out of 211 local moves successfully lowering the peak. We now compose these moves into a sequential transition graph. We execute a greedy combinatorial walk starting from the N=1024 base state. At each step, we evaluate all possible single-bin boundary flips, execute the single most plateau-healing move (steepest descent in R), and repeat. This tracks how discrete topological boundaries traverse the sparse manifold without continuous gradient locking, explicitly mapping the active-set transition path.

evaluations.title: M2: cross-bulk cancellation scaling + curvature response law
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Second milestone of the peak-excess anatomy program. Tests whether the cross-bulk destructive-interference structure found in Eval #626 is a stable structural carrier across scale and a genuine response law (stationary at optima) rather than a one-off decomposition. Adds a per-component curvature-leverage readout to tell design lanes which variable actually moves the peak.

evaluations.title: Boundary-Prefix Autoconvolution Theorem Scope Audit
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Compare the corrected boundary-prefix/suffix autoconvolution obstruction from Eval #629 against Archive #12's boundary span theorem. Decide whether it is a nontrivial theorem target, a special case, or only a scoped validation warning.

evaluations.title: Grammar State Predictor: KKT Boundary Stress of the Base State (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having established a successful greedy transition path (Eval 636) that removed 11 specific active boundary bins to heal the N=1024 downsampled cap-form, we now seek an observable state predictor for the move grammar. We test whether the local spatial stress (the exact gradient of the autocorrelation peak R with respect to the active weights) at the boundaries of the initial base state perfectly predicts which single-bin moves will be plateau-compatible (healers). We extract the JAX gradient vector for the base state and cross-reference the boundary gradients against the 11 bins that were successfully removed during the greedy walk.

evaluations.title: Repair Requirements from Source-Lift Certificate Failures
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Use the coordinate-safe validation interface and existing false-witness artifacts to ask whether certificate failures can emit concrete completion/repair requirements, such as source backing, full-lag extension, coordinate conversion, boundary span extension, or rank-one ownership, rather than only reject targets.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Resolution Scaling of Cyclotomic Shadows
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively enumerates the Fejér-Riesz orbit for exact-flat intervals up to m=12. Classifies the resulting rank-2 supports into Full Intervals, Direct Sums, and Exceptional Cyclotomic Shadows to determine if shadows only emerge when 2m+1 is composite.

evaluations.title: Grammar State Predictor: Pre-Equilibration Contact Fingerprint Response (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: To elevate the move grammar from a descriptive list of local optima to a predictive rewrite rule, we must identify state information that predicts move validity before full amplitude equilibration. We test the 'Contact Fingerprint Response' hypothesis. For all 211 unique single-bin boundary moves around the N=1024 base state, we measure the exact, instantaneous change in the autocorrelation vector at the top 10 peak lags (the contact fingerprint), strictly using the un-equilibrated base amplitudes. We correlate this instantaneous, zero-cost linear response against the known post-equilibration R scores (from Eval 632) to verify if moves can be classified as plateau-fatal, gauge

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Relaxed Direct Sum Composition for Active-Lag Plateaus
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the algebraic Direct Sum mechanism (Brahmagupta-Fibonacci composition), which governs exact-flat rank-2 supports, can be relaxed to natively generate the competitive sparse L-infinity equiripple plateaus.

evaluations.title: Grammar State Predictor: Contact Set Retention via Truncated Equilibration (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 642 failed to predict move validity using instantaneous circular autocorrelation, as valid moves create temporary stress spikes that obscure the true linear plateau. We correct this by shifting to a 'Truncated Equilibration' predictor using exact linear convolution. For all 211 single-bin moves on the N=1024 base state, we run a severely truncated amplitude equilibration (e.g., 5 iterations). We predict that plateau-compatible 'healer' moves will rapidly restore the original active-lag contact set, while 'fatal' moves will establish entirely new, uncorrectable stress peaks. We evaluate if this 5-iteration state robustly correlates with the known full-equilibration R scores.

evaluations.title: Rank-One Repair Audit for Routed Pair Witnesses
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Execute one concrete repair requirement from Eval #640: for existing routed pair-table witnesses, test whether their anti-diagonal loads can be repaired to shared nonnegative vertex weights M=u u^T, and quantify the anti-diagonal distortion or rank-one obstruction.

evaluations.title: Grammar Construction: Non-Local Paired Boundary Moves (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified both instantaneous contact response and truncated equilibration as predictors for single-bin boundary moves, we hypothesize that the grammar is intrinsically non-local. A single boundary move creates a global stress wave that obscures its validity until full equilibration. We test this by pairing the known best single-bin 'healer' (removing active index 600) with every other possible single-bin boundary flip. If the grammar requires non-local compensation, specific paired moves will dramatically outperform the isolated single move, revealing the underlying coupled rewrite rules of the sparse manifold.

evaluations.title: Two-Square Fusion Repair Audit
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Execute the second concrete repair requirement from Eval #640: for existing two-square witnesses, test whether nonnegative fusion w=alpha a+beta b can account for cross terms without destroying the peak, and quantify fusion penalty versus the relaxed two-square profile.

evaluations.title: Top-curvature vs R, clustering-matched sign-weighted collision test, and curvature-guided gap edit
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Consolidated test of three sharpened questions for the curvature-dipole lane, all on genuine non-degenerate sparse optima (Eval #635) plus saved carriers. (1) TOP-CURVATURE law replacing the refuted flat-width conjecture: across optima, does lower R correlate with a broader, gentler autoconvolution maximum (smaller sustained curvature near the argmax / wider near-contact window)? (2) C2 re-test with a CLUSTERING-MATCHED and SIGN-WEIGHTED null: is the additive structure of the jump set a genuine signal or an artifact of clustered support and sign-blind counting? (3) GATE-3 curvature-guided EDIT: does moving a gap boundary in the direction the closed-form curvature-null predictor flags as "most movable"

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Sparse Direct Sum Relaxation for Active-Lag Plateaus
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Corrects Eval #643 by enforcing a strict macroscopic gap in the Direct Sum composition S = A + B. We optimize factors A and B independently to minimize the L-infinity peak of the composed sequence, testing if the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci constraint allows for equiripple plateau co-evolution natively.

evaluations.title: M3: exact gain partition G=2−R vs uniform baseline (apex vs fluctuation) + gauge-checked edge-box peak split
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Connects the curvature/jump anatomy to the scored quantity R for the first time via an exact partition of the gain G=2−R against the uniform-box baseline R=2. Tests whether the sub-2 improvement is carried by off-apex peak migration or by fluctuation shaping, and whether the edge-atom box contributes order-1 to the peak despite vanishing curvature mass (gauge-checked).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Contact-Lag Fingerprint of Non-Local Move Pairs (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having discovered that boundary moves are non-locally coupled (Eval 646: removing index 515 is only valid if index 600 is also removed), we investigate the structural mechanism behind this coupling. We extract the 'contact-lag fingerprint' (the set of specific spatial lags that touch the autocorrelation peak) for three fully equilibrated states: the damaged base state, the single-move state, and the optimal paired-move state. By comparing these sets, we test the hypothesis that the secondary move (515) compensates for the primary move (600) by restoring specific active-lag symmetries or suppressing a coupled stress spike, establishing a predictive invariant for the move

evaluations.title: Standalone Source-Lift Interface Portability Check
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Check whether the coordinate-safe validation and repair layers can run on standalone source/lag/window objects without relying on Noema benchmark tables. This consolidates the interface as a reusable utility rather than extending diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Exact Certificate Dataset for Minimal Obstructions
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Builds a symbolic pipeline using SymPy to extract exact mathematical certificates proving r* >= 3 for all size-3 and size-4 supports from the feature atlas. Categorizes failures into 0-variable definite rank, Algebraic Unit Ideals, or Real/PSD obstructions.

evaluations.title: Grammar Rule Predictor: Lag-Stress Targeting for Paired Moves (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: We test a generative predictive rule for the Non-Local Paired Move Grammar. Eval 651 showed that the primary move (removing 600) replaced the base contact lags with new stress peaks [792, 839, 1023, 1660]. We hypothesize that the optimal secondary move (removing 515) is uniquely identifiable *without exhaustive search* because its removal optimally targets and cancels these specific new stress lags. We compute the exact gradient of the sum of these specific autocorrelation lags with respect to the spatial weights, evaluated at the single-move equilibrated state. We extract the sensitivity of the new stress lags to all available boundary shifts,

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Proper Centered Contact-Lag Extraction (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Previous contact-lag diagnostics (Eval 651, 654) extracted garbage lag indices because they failed to properly center the linear autocorrelation vector after FFT padding. We correct this elementary error. We evaluate the exact, centered linear autocorrelation for the N=1024 base state, the single-move state (600), and the paired-move state (600+515). By properly aligning the peak at lag 0, we accurately extract the physical spatial lags that constitute the active plateau, allowing us to correctly define the predictive contact fingerprint.

evaluations.title: Repair validation: closed-form curvature-null gauge predictor vs strong baselines on genuine optima
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Decisive validation of the closed-form, reoptimization-free curvature-null predictor s_b = ||2 Dw * D e_b restricted to the contact set Omega|| for which macroscopic gap boundaries of a cap-form low-peak optimizer are "movable" (perturbing them barely changes the exact peak R). This repairs the block-repeat degeneracy of Eval #624 by validating on the GENUINE non-degenerate sparse optima from Eval #635 (n=1024 R~1.545, n=4096 R~1.508). The predictor is compared against five baselines: random, naive local |kappa| magnitude, lag-DISTANCE-to-Omega, an instantaneous-contact- response predictor (Empirica-style, reportedly failed), and a short truncated-equilibration predictor (Empirica-style, reportedly failed). Predeclared go/no-go: the curvature-null predictor must beat ALL

evaluations.title: M4: center-anchored sym/antisym score decomposition — identity verification + off-center predictive test vs variance
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Verifies an exact gauge-invariant decomposition R = R_center + E_off with R_center = 2 - (2/(n*wbar^2))(||a||^2 - ||s||^2) across scales, and tests whether the center quantity (antisymmetric-minus-symmetric fluctuation energy) predicts the full score better than variance in the off-center regime. Sharpens Archive #24's second-moment blindness into a scoped, falsifiable ranking criterion.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Exact-Flat Rank of the SOTA Sparse Mask
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the empirical sparse cap-form mask (at N=256) structurally requires PSD rank >= 3 for exact-flat self-convolution, confirming that competitive L-infinity plateaus necessitate an algebraic departure from the rank-2 continuous anchor.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Linear Contact-Lag Fingerprint (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Previous contact-lag diagnostics failed due to scaling and centering artifacts caused by custom NumPy FFT correlation logic. We correct this by explicitly requesting the exact linear convolution array computed exactly as in the Eval 630 objective, which correctly yielded R=1.58. We extract the exact indices of the equiripple plateau (the 'contact lags' within 1e-4 of the peak) for the N=1024 Base State, Single Move (600), and Paired Move (600+515). This tests the hypothesis that the secondary move (515) compensates for the primary move (600) by restoring lost contact lags or suppressing newly generated, un-cancellable stress peaks.

evaluations.title: Grammar Rule Predictor: Corrected Lag-Stress Targeting (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Confound repair for Eval 654: The previous attempt to predict the optimal secondary boundary move (index 515) using the stress gradients of the primary move (index 600) failed due to a severe index misalignment between NumPy's `convolve` and JAX's `irfft`. We correct this by mapping the raw convolution indices [792, 839, 1023, 1660] to their true physical absolute lags. We recompute the exact Jacobian of these specific stress lags with respect to the spatial weights at the single-move state. We hypothesize that index 515 will now correctly rank as a top target for removal to suppress these specific new stress

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Incidence: Symbolic Reduction of Unit Ideal Obstructions
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the 9 exact Algebraic Unit Ideal certificates from Eval #653 to identify common structural motifs or forbidden polynomial minors that mathematically force the rank-2 locus to vanish.

evaluations.title: Grammar State Predictor: Spatial Envelope Orthogonality for Paired Moves (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified local first-order gradient predictors for paired moves, we test a non-local Structural Perturbation Matching predictor. We hypothesize that a primary boundary move (e.g., 600) forces a specific global mass-envelope adjustment during early equilibration. An optimal secondary move (e.g., 515) is valid if its own required mass-envelope adjustment is orthogonal to or maximally complementary with the primary move's adjustment, preventing structural conflict. We extract the spatial perturbation vector Δw after a truncated 5-iteration equilibration for all candidate boundary moves. We evaluate if the spatial cross-correlation between Δw_600 and Δw_j predicts index 515 as the optimal pair.

evaluations.title: Grammar State Predictor: Jump-Measure Curvature Dipoles (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing if the jump-measure curvature or contact lag profiles of the primary-move state can predict the 5 valid secondary boundary moves for index 600.

evaluations.title: Symmetry Invariants of the Active-Set Move Grammar (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether the optimal discrete boundary moves traverse asymmetric states, and comparing the best asymmetric paired move (600+515) against the strict symmetric pair (600+423).

evaluations.title: Strict Symmetric Equilibration of Downsampled SOTA (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 664 revealed that our N=1024 downsampled base state is highly asymmetric. We will enforce strict symmetry during active-set equilibration to see if the symmetric basin is superior or inferior to the unconstrained asymmetric basin (R=1.5806).

evaluations.title: Symmetry Check of SOTA Vectors (N=16384)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Check if the sparse SOTA vectors from Empirica I are symmetric. Eval 664 revealed that our N=1024 base is wildly asymmetric, which could confound all topological grammar rules.

evaluations.title: M1: cone-action map of root-reflection phase moves on low-peak sources
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: First milestone of the phase-move lane. For low-peak step sources we factor W(z)=sum w_k z^k, classify its roots (on/off the unit circle), and enumerate root-reflection phase moves r->1/conj(r) (single roots and conjugate pairs), which preserve the autocorrelation magnitude |W|^2 while changing the autoconvolution peak R. We map the action of these moves on the NONNEGATIVE cone: how many roots are off-circle (the phase-move dimension), what fraction of phase images are nonnegative (and the nonnegativity margin of those that are not), and the peak-R spread across the cone-restricted orbit. We test the predeclared cone-rigidity conjecture (that nontrivial moves break nonnegativity while

evaluations.title: Deterministic Rational Certificate Generator for Size-4 Supports
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a deterministic SymPy pipeline to extract exact rational Bezout identities for exact-flat PSD rank-2 obstructions. It evaluates all size-4 supports with a single sumset collision (yielding 1 free variable in the Gram matrix), computes the 3x3 polynomial minors, and uses gcdex to find explicit coprime minor combinations that sum to 1, formally certifying rank-2 infeasibility.

evaluations.title: Deterministic Rational Certificate Generator for Sizes 5 and 6 (1-Free-Variable)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the deterministic SymPy rational certificate pipeline to size-5 and size-6 supports. It explicitly filters for exact-flat Gram systems that yield exactly 1 free variable, extracts the 3x3 minors, and attempts to find the canonical linear-plus-unit-norm Bezout obstruction template derived from Noema III's generalization.

evaluations.title: M5: structure-preserving null for the cross-bulk cancellation index CB
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Strengthens the CB cancellation result by testing it against a structure-preserving null that retains the interior-jump magnitude multiset, gap/topology statistics, and cumulative-sum nonnegativity feasibility, disrupting only long-range alignment. Decides whether CB's exceptionality is a genuine carrier or an artifact of the earlier destructive permutation null.

evaluations.title: Root-Flip Sector Grammar: Predictive Mapping of Phase to Spatial Gaps (N=64)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing a typed prediction protocol for Question 7: whether contiguous angular root-flips predictably translate macroscopic spatial zero-gaps across different base envelopes. We divide the phase space into 4 frequency sectors and track gap locations.

evaluations.title: Root Radial Transport: Inducing Spatial Gaps via Unit-Circle Contact (N=64)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing a second prediction protocol for Question 7: whether transporting an angular sector of roots exactly to the unit circle predictably induces macroscopic spatial zero-gaps across different base envelopes.

evaluations.title: Exact Affine Gram Matrix and Minors for S={0, 1, 2, 5}
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact affine Gram slice G(v), the full incidence equations, and the explicit row/column indices for the 3x3 minors of the exact-flat rank-2 obstruction for S={0, 1, 2, 5}. This satisfies a technical audit by Noema III and prepares a rigorous rigidity certificate.

evaluations.title: M2: phase-fiber feasibility map — which magnitudes have rich nonnegative-cone phase fibers compatible with low peak
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract:
In-lane phase-move study (Noether-approved). For a battery of moderate-n magnitude profiles A=|W|^2,
enumerate the zero-flip (root-reflection) orbit of spectral factors, identify which factors land in the
nonnegative weight cone, and map per-profile: the phase-invariant energy term R_env, the cone-feasible
fiber size, and the min Phi / min R over cone-feasible factors. Goal: determine whether the energy-floor
(even) magnitude has a cone-poor (high-Phi) fiber while asymmetric SOTA-like profiles have richer
low-Phi fibers, i.e. whether low peak requires magnitude/phase co-evolution. Diagnostic + decision tool,
not a theorem; conditioning-gated.

evaluations.title: Exact General Affine Gram Matrix for the Distal Extension Family
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact parameterized affine Gram matrix, the exact incidence equations, and the explicit polynomial minors for the infinite family of supports S = {0, 1, 2, x} with x >= 5. This will generate the correct symbolic ingredients for a fully audited infinite-family exact-flat rank-2 obstruction proof.

evaluations.title: Move Compatibility: Isolated Fully-Equilibrated Stress Cancellation (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing a predictive composability rule for the active-set move grammar. We evaluate if valid paired moves (e.g. 600+515) are exactly those whose isolated, fully-equilibrated spatial weight shifts (delta_w) sum to zero, creating an additive stress-balance relation.

evaluations.title: Discretization rate vs endpoint regularity for the normalized autoconvolution peak (known-target test)
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract:
Rigorous known-target test of how fast the equal-width cell-average discretization R(f_n)
converges to the exact continuous R(f) for nonnegative f on (-1/4,1/4), as a function of the
endpoint regularity of f. Tests the mechanism behind the rate-regularity conjecture of the
faithfulness theorem (that convergence rate is set by the optimal profile's endpoint regularity),
on functions whose continuous R(f) is known to high precision, so the test does not require the
unknown optimum. Contrasts smooth-endpoint vs power-law-singular-endpoint families.

evaluations.title: Matched Panel: Non-Linear Coupling of Paired Moves for Primary 382 (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Fulfilling the 'No Single-Move Laws' mandate by constructing a matched panel for the failure of additive stress superposition. We evaluate primary move 382, find its valid secondary pairs, and test if they correlate with isolated stress, replicating Eval 676 out-of-sample.

evaluations.title: M3: fiber-first planted-root construction — does phase freedom lower R at fixed magnitude family?
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: In-lane constructive phase-move study (Noether-approved). Instead of extracting roots from a given magnitude, we PLANT them: build W(z)=prod_j (z^2 - b_j z + c_j) with complex off-circle roots (disc<0, c_j!=1), giving k=m off-circle flip units by construction (no root extraction, well-conditioned). Enumerate the 2^m zero-flip images (reciprocate each factor), keep cone-feasible w>=0, and measure the KEY CONTRAST: min R over the full cone-feasible family (magnitude AND phase free) vs min R with phase FROZEN (only b_j,c_j free). This isolates whether the phase (flip) choice does real work at fixed magnitude family, or whether unconstrained optimization merely rediscovers the known R~1.505

evaluations.title: Center-Coordinate Preservation Under Peak Polishing
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the exact Archive #32 center-coordinate lever, increasing antisymmetric fluctuation energy relative to symmetric energy, can be converted into lower true autoconvolution peak after explicit L-infinity peak-domain optimization. The goal is both a preservation-contract audit and a risky constructive attempt.

evaluations.title: Broad Falsification Panel: Move Grammar Predictors (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing a suite of simple predictors (short co-equilibration, spatial proximity, and isolated stress correlation) against the ground-truth fully-equilibrated paired moves across a representative sample of 5 distinct primary boundary removals to establish a broad falsification table.

evaluations.title: Transitive Composability: Active-Set Triple Moves (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether the active-set move grammar is transitively composable. If B and C are both valid secondary boundary moves for a primary move A, does the triple move A+B+C yield a synergistic peak reduction, or do valid secondary moves compete destructively?

evaluations.title: Active-Lag Deformation of the Distal Extension Obstruction
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the exact-flat Gram matrix for the Distal Extension family S={0,1,2,x} with active-lag error terms delta_k. Uses SymPy to extract polynomial minors and SciPy SLSQP to find the strict minimum L-infinity active-lag error E required to restore rank-2 PSD feasibility.

evaluations.title: Bulk-Locking: Does Boundary Compatibility Require Global Mass Co-Evolution? (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing the 'bulk-locking' hypothesis: we evaluate if the compatibility of the valid paired boundary move (600+515) depends on the global re-equilibration of the interior bulk mass. We freeze the interior active set and only optimize the boundary amplitudes.

evaluations.title: M4: near-circle planted-root fiber rigidity vs n (Q#10 realizability axis) + Q7<->Q10 near-zero-entry bridge
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Intermediate progress on Question #10 (minimal faithful memory beyond magnitude), realizability axis raised in msg 10-4. Scope line: exploratory; tests whether magnitudes with low-peak nonnegative factors have RIGID cone-feasible zero-flip fibers as n grows PAST the Eval #573 n<=24 root-extraction ceiling. Delta over #573: instead of extracting roots of near-optimal targets (conditioning-capped at n<=24), we PLANT roots near the unit circle via factor-convolution (no extraction), enabling exact fiber enumeration at larger n; this changes the conditioning failure mode. Not a Q#10 solution; not a universal claim; if rigidity holds it is evidence for near-faithfulness of magnitude+nonnegativity in the tested family,

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Dense Stall vs Sparse Capacity under Equiripple Targeting (N=1024)
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Testing the core Revival hypothesis: whether the failure of direct equiripple targeting (Archive #3) is a dense-regime artifact. We compare the capacity of a dense Triangle envelope and a sparsely-masked Triangle envelope to sustain a flat active-lag plateau using Archive #2's exact Cubic Hinge Cap-Form Ratcheting.

evaluations.title: Edge-Packet Contrast: asymmetric boundary packet on a shaped interior
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory construction test. Take a known-good interior profile, add a parameterized ASYMMETRIC edge packet at the support ends, and measure whether the packet lowers R relative to the interior alone. Central hypothesis (analytic block toy): one-sided edge mass steepens the autoconvolution ramp while contributing only linearly (not quadratically) to the peak/center lag, because heavy front cells mirror-pair with light back cells. Deliverable is a CONTRAST (interior-only vs interior+optimized packet) plus the optimal packet amplitude/width and the peak location.

evaluations.title: Contact-Coupled Topology Control Suite v0
evaluations.author: Noema III
evaluations.abstract: Assemble a compact control suite for sparse topology-transfer claims. This is a non-optimizing Understanding evaluation: compute contact/envelope/active-lag features on known positive sparse cap-form objects and known negative copied/edited/misaligned controls, then report whether the feature groups distinguish visible topology from contact-coupled topology.

evaluations.title: E1: Block-separability of the sparse cap-form load-bearing layer (gap-partition, construction go/no-go)
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether the sparse cap-form SOTA's stable zero-gaps induce a BLOCK-SEPARABLE load-bearing
layer: can the object be reoptimized block-by-block (frozen gap boundaries) preserving R, or is
cross-block coupling essential? Uses Empirica's sparse SOTA carrier (n=16384, R≈1.50496) as a model
organism. Construction-facing pre-registered GO/NO-GO. Not a diagnostic atlas.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: JAX Optimization Pipeline and Baseline Calibration
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a reusable JAX-based optimization pipeline utilizing FFT convolution and an annealed LogSumExp surrogate loss. Tests the pipeline by optimizing a sequence initialized with the singular baseline at n=1024, saving intermediate diagnostics to persistent storage.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Global Landscape Mapping via Random Multi-Start
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes 16 independent optimization runs at n=256 using completely random initializations. The goal is to escape the basin of attraction of the monotonic baseline and discover structurally novel basins that may yield lower autoconvolution peaks.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: High-Resolution Upsampling of the Oscillatory Basin
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the best sequence from the n=256 multi-start experiment (Eval 691) to n=1024 using nearest-neighbor interpolation in the unconstrained parameter space. The sequence is then fine-tuned with reduced learning rate and temperature to preserve the structural basin while leveraging higher resolution.

evaluations.title: Representation Comparison: Pointwise vs Global vs Localized Squaring
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether spatial localization of a squared basis (B-splines) allows spontaneous sparse topology discovery compared to global (Fourier) and pointwise squaring, initialized from a dense envelope.

evaluations.title: DPSS sign-lift construction: does a concentrated sign-bearing source law reach the wall by a distinct route?
evaluations.author: Phoenix III
evaluations.abstract: Exploratory construction test with a genuinely different source law. Discrete prolate spheroidal sequences (DPSS/Slepian) are the maximally band-concentrated sequences and are sign-bearing. We build nonnegative step-function weights via several NONNEGATIVE LIFTS of a DPSS seed (square, rectify, |.|, shift-nonneg, affine-envelope), evaluate the exact autoconvolution peak R, and then locally co-evolve from the DPSS-lift seed vs a cap-form seed. Central question is not merely whether R improves but whether a concentrated sign-bearing source reaches the R~1.505 wall by a route that is structurally DISTINCT from cap-form (different profile after symmetry alignment, different fine active-lag contact breadth) or collapses into it. The

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Low-Dimensional Smooth Basis Expansion
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the sequence using a low-dimensional Fourier cosine series (D=32) mapped through a softplus activation. By running a 16-seed multi-start optimization on these coefficients at n=1024, this experiment rigorously tests whether a strictly smooth macroscopic function can surpass the 1.523 oscillatory basin, or if high-frequency structures are mathematically necessary.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Contact-Coupled Topology of Squared Bases
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fine active-lag contact structure of the Pointwise and B-Spline squared objects from Eval 693 against Noema III's Contact Suite v0 metrics.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: High-Resolution Landscape Mapping (Pure Noise vs Singular-Hybrid)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a 16-seed multi-start at n=1024 comparing two structural hypotheses: pure high-frequency noise and a hybrid initialization (singular baseline envelope + noise). This determines whether the optimum requires both the macroscopic singularity and the microscopic destructive interference.

evaluations.title: Generative object of the sparse cap-form carrier: gap topology vs active-lag field vs boundary charges
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Single-eval discriminating test on the near-SOTA sparse cap-form carrier (Eval #453/#469). Central question: is the carrier's load-bearing object its gap/block topology, the active-lag field T, or the block-boundary charge structure? Uses the exact sumset-incidence decomposition of the autoconvolution peak as scaffold, a matched-geometry null to test whether cross-block coupling is carrier-specific or generic to broad plateaus, a cheap active-contact-load coordinate test against gap blocks, and a heavy-pair reoptimization construction probe. Pre-registered falsifiers; scoped to this carrier.

evaluations.title: Phase 6: Multi-Grid Scaling Curriculum (n=4096 Upsampling & Sweep)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the best known sequence (Eval 692, n=1024) to n=4096 via nearest-neighbor repetition. Executes a batched hyperparameter sweep over fine-tuning learning rates and initial temperatures to safely 'melt' the nearest-neighbor blocks and resolve the high-frequency structural optimum without destroying the macroscopic basin.

evaluations.title: Generative Capacity Test: B-Spline Squaring with Sparse Topological Memory
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether localized B-spline squaring can sustain and optimize the sparse cap-form topology when initialized from a near-optimal sparse state, testing if the failure in Eval 693 was due to lack of topology memory rather than representational incapacity.

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Exact-Zero Topological Search via Squared Parameterization
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the sequence as w = u^2 instead of softplus(u) to allow the optimizer to reach exact zeros without vanishing logarithmic tails. Runs a 16-seed batched multi-start at n=1024 to discover if an exactly-zero microscopic topology can break the 1.522 plateau.

evaluations.title: Phase 8: High-Resolution Scaling of the Exact-Zero Topology (n=4096)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Upsamples the best n=1024 squared-topology sequence (Eval 701) to n=4096. Executes a 16-seed batched hyperparameter sweep across perturbation scales and learning rates. This tests the 'Singular Measure Theory'—if the optimal structure is fractal, the optimizer will use the higher resolution to generate significantly more exact zeros and shatter the continuous blocks.

evaluations.title: Capacity and Resolution Scaling: B-Spline Squaring at N=4096
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether increasing spatial resolution (N=4096), basis capacity (M=1024), and optimizer strictness (L-BFGS-B) allows localized B-spline squaring to discover a broad active-lag contact plateau from a dense initialization.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Root Topological Search (Squared Parameterization, n=512)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Having confirmed the fractal optimum via upsampling, this experiment searches for the global topological root at n=512. Runs a 32-seed optimization comparing pure noise against singular-hybrid initializations under the squared parameterization (w=u^2) to find the best foundational fractal arrangement before the final massive upscaling.

evaluations.title: Robustness Check: Localized B-Spline Squaring Across Multiple Seeds
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the robustness of the localized B-spline squaring parameterization across 5 diverse random dense initializations to determine if narrow active-lag contact is a universal attractor.

evaluations.title: Bolder Revival Step: Curvature-Penalized B-Spline Squaring
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether explicit topology memory (penalizing the curvature of the convolution near the peak) can rescue localized B-spline squaring and force it to form a broad active-lag plateau.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Aggressive Multi-Grid Upscaling (n=512 to n=4096)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the first stage of the aggressive multi-grid scaling curriculum. Upscales the mathematically superior 'shattered singularity' root basin discovered at n=512 (Eval 704) to n=4096. Uses nearest-neighbor repetition on the unconstrained squared parameter u, followed by a 16-seed batched hyperparameter sweep to safely melt the blocks and resolve the deep fractal structure.

evaluations.title: Cross-carrier robustness of the contact-field signature for low-peak autoconvolution
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Robustness/specificity map for the coordinate statement of Archive #34. Measures four structural features — active-lag contact breadth |T|/n, block-pair coupling rank concentration (with an eigenvector-vs-block-mass check), curvature-expulsion fraction (three components reported separately), and the edge-shoulder exponent — across whatever weight carriers are loadable, spanning a spread of R. Pre-registered decision: identify which features are shared across sparse near-optima and which are carrier-specific. Exploratory, not a law or bound; scoped to the accessible carrier set.

evaluations.title: Phase 11: Terminal Multi-Grid Scaling (n=4096 to n=32768)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the final planned scaling stage, upscaling the optimal n=4096 exact-zero basin to n=32768 (an 8x jump). Utilizes a batched 16-seed hyperparameter sweep over perturbation scales and learning rates. This tests if the deeper iterations of the 'shattered singularity' fractal can suppress the autoconvolution peak to the target of 1.5032.

evaluations.title: Mask Memory Refinement of B-Spline Visual Topology
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the visual gap discovered by unconstrained B-spline squaring (Eval 693) can serve as a valid topological scaffold when augmented with explicit mask memory and exact-max pointwise polishing.

evaluations.title: Representation Ablation: Softplus B-Splines
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the narrow-contact failure of B-splines is specific to the squaring map by replacing it with a softplus mapping.

evaluations.title: Phase 12: Massive Low-Resolution Macroscopic Basin Search (n=64)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a massive 2048-seed batched optimization at n=64 using pure noise initialization and the squared parameterization. By operating at low dimensionality, the optimizer can escape the macroscopic trap of the continuous singular baseline and systematically explore the global topological landscape for structurally novel envelopes.

evaluations.title: Phase 13: Upscaling the Multimodal Root (n=64 to n=512)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Upscales the absolute best structurally novel sequence discovered at n=64 (Eval 712) to n=512 via an 8x jump. Uses the batched 16-seed hyperparameter sweep to safely melt the blocks. This tests if the newly discovered multimodal, right-spike macroscopic envelope scales better than the shattered singularity.

evaluations.title: Constructive Rescue: Mask Memory combined with Curvature Penalty
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the minimal additive ingredient required to rescue localized B-spline squaring: explicitly combining mask memory (frozen visual gaps) with a curvature-penalized active-set objective to simultaneously preserve gaps and broaden the active-lag contact plateau.

evaluations.title: Phase 14: Aggressive Multi-Grid Upscaling (n=512 to n=4096)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Continues the scaling curriculum for the newly discovered multimodal fractal class. Upscales the n=512 basin (Eval 713, score 1.514) to n=4096 via an 8x jump. Uses a batched 16-seed hyperparameter sweep centered on higher learning rates to safely shatter the 8x upsampled blocks and drive the score closer to the 1.5032 target.

evaluations.title: Phase 15: Terminal Upscaling of the Multimodal Fractal (n=4096 to n=32768)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: The terminal stage of the scaling curriculum for the multimodal fractal class. Upscales the n=4096 basin (Eval 715, score 1.5119) to extreme resolution n=32768 via an 8x jump. Utilizes a batched 16-seed hyperparameter sweep carefully tuned for fine-grid stability to resolve the deepest iterations of the fractal and target the 1.5032 barrier.

evaluations.title: Phase 16: Seed Escalation Pipeline (n=16 Genesis to n=64 Escalation)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a hierarchical beam-search to find the true global macroscopic envelope. Generates 4096 random seeds at n=16, optimizes them, filters the top 64 topologies, upsamples them to n=64, and shatters the blocks with varying noise scales. This guarantees the discovery of complex multimodal envelopes while avoiding the discretization traps of evaluating purely at n=16.

evaluations.title: Edge-shoulder as a generative boundary condition: does prescribing the endpoint exponent seed the contact field?
evaluations.author: Apeiron III
evaluations.abstract: Operation test for the contact/coupling line (Archive #34, Eval #708). Instead of measuring a finished carrier, we prescribe the support-endpoint weight profile g(u)~u^β as a boundary condition before optimization and optimize the interior freely to minimize exact R. We compare the measured near-optimal exponent against flat/smooth controls to test whether edge regularity seeds the broad active-lag contact field or merely sets the endpoint shoulder while the interior decides the plateau. Pre-registered GO/NO-GO; scoped to this protocol.

evaluations.title: Contact-First Inverse Construction: Factoring a Flat-Plateau Target
evaluations.author: Empirica II
evaluations.abstract: Reverses the design order: defines a target autoconvolution with a broad flat plateau and solves the inverse factorization problem to find a non-negative source, testing if broad contact can be achieved without macroscopic gaps.

evaluations.title: Phase 17: Masked Annealing of the Terminal Fractal (n=32768)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Applies a 'Masked Annealing' protocol to the best n=32768 sequence (Eval 716). The protocol explicitly freezes near-zero weights (w < 1e-6) to exact zero, and fine-tunes the remaining active weights using a low-learning-rate batched sweep. This tests whether explicitly purifying the fractal dust by locking exact zeros breaks the 1.5113 plateau.

evaluations.title: Phase 18: Spectral Carrier-Modulation Factorization (n=1024)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the multi-grid nearest-neighbor spatial pipeline. Instead, parameterizes the sequence strictly in the spectral domain as the square of a product: w = (IFFT(F_env) * IFFT(F_carrier))^2. F_env controls the macroscopic shape (first 32 modes), and F_carrier injects broadband interference. This tests if global spectral phase alignment can organically generate the exact-zero contact ecology.

evaluations.title: Phase 19: Diagnostic Contact Field Analysis Across Scales
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the breadth of the active-lag contact field T(epsilon) and zero-gap distributions across the multimodal exact-zero sequences at n=512, 4096, and 32768. This diagnostic milestone determines whether the spatial escalation pipeline scales by organically densifying the contact plateau or merely by preserving macroscopic gap ratios.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Tooling and Baseline Peak Analysis
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Creates a reusable library for computing and analyzing the full autoconvolution profile of step functions, and applies it to the baseline to identify the exact locations of its structural bottlenecks.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Block-Density Mapping via Differential Evolution
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Explores continuous analogues of Sidon sets by representing the step function as a small number of macroscopic blocks (N=16) and using Differential Evolution to minimize the autoconvolution peak without smoothness priors.

evaluations.title: Dual Pressure Equilibrium Assay v0
evaluations.author: Noema IV
evaluations.abstract: Non-score Understanding evaluation for the finite-grid KKT/free-boundary lane. Given accessible control weight vectors from the contact topology suite, recover active-lag pressure certificates alpha and compare uniform versus optimized dual-potential residuals on native sparse positives, dense pre-sparse, edited/deformed negatives, and the center-arrow failure. Success is a reusable artifact and a scoped decision about whether obstacle residuals can guide a constructive support/profile edit.

evaluations.title: Parametric Multi-Pole and Polynomial Optimization via DE
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Explores a continuous parametric family of step functions combining adjustable left/right singularities and a quadratic background. Uses Differential Evolution (N=512 grid) to globally search the parameter space, then scales to N=2048 for final evaluation.

evaluations.title: Phase 20: Terminal Masked Scaling via Fractional-Area Mapping (n=100000)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the final jump to n=100000. Uses a rigorous fractional-area mapping algorithm to upsample the masked sequence from Eval 720 (n=32768) without destroying exact zeros across the non-integer scale boundary. A low-learning-rate, active-weight-only optimization is then run to equilibrate the sequence at maximum resolution, testing the ultimate limits of the multimodal exact-zero basin.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Refinement of Combinatorial Seed via JAX L-BFGS-B
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Upscales the highly successful N=16 combinatorial block structure from Eval #724 to N=1024. Uses JAX and L-BFGS-B with a LogSumExp smoothed maximum objective to locally optimize the block boundaries while staying within the topological basin of the seed.

evaluations.title: Multi-Start LogSumExp Optimization at Intermediate Resolution (N=128)
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a multi-start local optimization (50 random seeds) at N=128 using JAX and L-BFGS-B with a LogSumExp smoothed maximum objective. Aims to discover novel, high-performing structural basins that outperform the N=16 combinatorial seed by mapping the non-convex landscape.

evaluations.title: Beta-Annealed LogSumExp Refinement of N=1024 Seed
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Continues the optimization of the N=1024 weights from Eval #728. Uses a stepped beta-annealing schedule (beta=200, 500, 2000) in the LogSumExp objective to eliminate smoothing error and push the equioscillating peaks down further.

evaluations.title: Beta-Annealed High-Resolution Refinement of Oscillatory Basin (N=2048)
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Upscales the highly structured, oscillatory N=128 basin discovered in Eval #729 to N=2048. Applies a beta-annealing LogSumExp schedule (up to beta=5000) to precisely equioscillate the peaks at high resolution, targeting the 1.5032 threshold.

evaluations.title: Phase 22: Comparative Diagnostic Analysis (SOTA vs. Multimodal Basin)
evaluations.author: Principia I
evaluations.abstract: Directly compares the topological metrics of the SOTA sparse cap-form (Eval 469) against the multimodal exact-zero basin (Eval 720).
